When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Warning! Spoilers ahead for Season 9, Episode 5 of FBI, “Atonement,” streaming now with a Paramount+ subscription.

FBI may be in its ninth season on the 2026 TV schedule, but the series continues to keep fans on the edge of their seats. Following OA’s undercover storyline, one would think that things are back to normal at 26 Fed. Unfortunately, there may be another shakeup coming. After the end of this week’s episode, I’m worried that another major exit is near.

Throughout the Dick Wolf CBS procedural’s run, there have been a handful of exits. In the last couple of years, FBI has seen three big departures. It seemed like the curse could be done after Juliana Aidén Martinez’s addition at the beginning of Season 8, but alas, another could be coming.

In this week’s episode, “Atonement,” Scola (John Boyd) told the team that Nina (Shantel VanSanten) was offered to run her own task force. It was great news, but Scola didn’t seem too sure about it. He later tells Eva (Aidén Martinez) that the job is in San Diego. While at first he told Nina not to take it, he eventually calls her to say that she should after his conversation with Eva.

Scola was scared about uprooting their life and moving across the country, which is why he told Nina not to take it in the first place. His hesitation is understandable. He’s lived in New York his entire life, their son, Dougie, is getting older, and he has his job. That being said, Nina’s worked hard to get to where she is, and it’s a great promotion for her, which is why Scola came to his senses and told her she should take it. They’ll figure it out.

Whether Boyd is actually leaving FBI remains unknown. VanSanten is set to return to the series on Monday, November 16, but little has been shared about the episode beyond the fact that the team will work alongside Nina to intercept a criminal on the Most Wanted list. Scola and Nina have gone through a lot over the last several seasons, between breakups, makeups, near-deaths, and welcoming their son. While I would absolutely hate to say goodbye to Scola, it would only make sense for him to follow Nina to San Diego so they can stay together and raise their son in the same proximity and not 2,800 miles apart.

Nothing is confirmed, and it’s not even clear if Nina will end up taking the job. It’s likely we’ll get more information during VanSanten’s return on November 16, but fans may have to brace themselves. Boyd has been on FBI since Season 2. It’s hard to imagine the show without him, but at this point, unfortunately, anything is possible. For now, we’ll just have to wait and see. New episodes of FBI air on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

#3818. Yakuza creator's new studio and its debut game Gang of Dragon are no more after losing funding from NetEase

Nagoshi Studio has officially shut down and its first game called Gang of Dragon is seemingly no more, months after publisher NetEase pulled funding from the Yakuza-like project.

Toshihiro Nagoshi (often cited as the creator of the brilliant Yakuza and Like A Dragon game series) opened his new studio in 2021 and announced his next game with a very familiar title almost one year ago. Now, the Tokyo-based developer has closed its doors, as confirmed in the Japanese government gazette Kanpo.

The news comes months after employees were told that the studio's future was at risk due to NetEase's funding cuts. Nagoshi Studio reportedly needed another £33.1 million (about $44.4m at the time) to get Gang of Dragon past the finish line - a paycheck NetEase purportedly didn't want to cough up.

The China-based Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet publisher has been significantly scaling back on international investments these past few years. Visions of Mana developer Ouka Studios was shut down just after launching its gorgeous action game, Worlds Untold (a studio formed by Mass Effect veteran Mac Walters) had to pause operations to find a new partner, and Halo Infinite lead Jerry Hook's studio also ran into very similar issues last year.

Some developers have been a little luckier. Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture saved itself with a management buyout and now operates as an independent developer, for one.

Not much is known about Gang of Dragon, but its debut trailer featured the violent crime and high drama you'd expect from Nagoshi's previous work. The game also starred Ma Dong-seok, the acclaimed actor you might recognise from films such as Train to Busan and Marvel's Eternals.

#3817. RAM-devouring AI overlord Sam Altman says he totally doesn’t want your memory, claims statement ‘was taken out of context’

After claiming people having RAM was “quite terrible” and rightfully getting dunked on by a huge part of the internet, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said his controversial statement was “taken out of context” in a post today.

“I actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context,” Altman wrote on social media (as spotted by Kotaku). “I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time,” the CEO added.

Despite his claims, the statement in question seems pretty clear-cut. “From a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time,”Altman said in an interview last week. “You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment.”

but only because…i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context.i have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

AI companies like OpenAI play a huge hand in the skyrocketing RAM prices, since they vaccuum up available RAM and shrink the available supply. But don’t worry, Altman said he doesn’t want to steal your memory; instead, he said he just wants the world to build more RAM—probably so he doesn’t have to covet yours in the first place.

Altman’s original statement unsurprisingly went up like a lead balloon, earning him ridicule from the internet. “Using a stick of RAM to stir my coffee this morning, fuck you, Sam Altman,” one user wrote. Another image—which prompted Altman’s response—had a series of RAM sticks laid out toward a box trap. “I lol’d,” the OpenAI CEO said eloquently.

To show he’s a funny, harmless guy who can take a joke and is totally not making cartoonishly large eyes at your RAM sticks, Sam Altman changed his social media name to “Ram Altman,” Kotaku reports, though he has changed it back at the time of writing.

Last week, stock prices for big tech companies plummeted after they reported suboptimal earnings. Google in particular purportedly pointed to its AI overview hurting its bottom line.

AI has been nearly ubiquitous in the past years. It “has infested the world as no parasite had ever done before,” as Destructoid’s Andrej Barovic put it, dealing devastating environmental, economic, and societal blows to the world. But the technology gives us undoubtedly good things, like making fun of how atrocious DLSS 5 looks and… yeah, I think that’s it.

It sorta looks like it's in three dimensions!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Remember the 3D craze? The Nintendo 3DS, 3D TV, 3D cinema; it was a new, exciting technology that some expected would go mainstream one day. Then the dream just sorta died. People don't talk about it much these days; except for this wonderful project that takes normal videos and turns them, alchemy-like, into slightly more 3D-looking videos using the Steam Frame.

And let me tell you, it's actually pretty good.

It's called framedepth, and it's made by a user going by guix8 on GitHub. It's a plugin for Chrome that adds a stereoscopic 3D effect to any video when viewed via the browser on the Steam Frame.

It's surprisingly fun. I've been watching live gigs and eating challenges on YouTube and the stereoscopic effect is automatically applied once enabled via the extension. It definitely adds some extra level of immersion to it. Not much, but some. I wouldn't go as far to say I felt like I was there in the crowd for either spectacle, and maybe I wouldn't want to be in the firing line of a food challenge, but it's better than I thought it would be. An ever-so-slightly more engaging way to watch YouTube in VR.

The installation process is a bit more involved than your average Chrome plugin, requiring the Steam Frame to be in developer mode. You need to install Chrome on the Steam Frame, which requires a quick trip to the SteamOS desktop to run the Konsole and install via Flathub (flatpak install com.google.Chrome). Then you have to download framedepth from the GitHub and whack more code in the terminal:

cd ~/Downloads && f=$(ls -v framedepth-*-steamos-arm64.tar.gz | tail -1) && echo "$f" # the newest download

sha256sum -c "$f.sha256" && tar -xzf "$f" && cd "${f%.tar.gz}"

bash install.sh # ~/.local/share/framedepth, user service, extension files

Finally, it needs to be loaded as an extension into Chrome, which also requires developer mode to be enabled for extensions in the browser. Once installed, you can enable the 3D effect and change the settings from a dropdown menu right there in Chrome.

The pop-out slider to the max seems to have the most impact on the 3D effect; the equivalent of cranking the 3DS slider all the way up.

There's a bunch to play around with here, but it's worth a go if you have a Steam Frame. If anything, just to rekindle lost excitement for 3D technologies that never managed to win us all over.

"For future growth, we have to attach great importance to our new platform," says chief financial officer Lin Tao

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sony says that work on its "next-generation platform" – AKA the PS6 – is "progressing as scheduled," while sales of the PS5 keep on trucking, but at a pace that's lagging behind the PS4 at the same point in its own lifecycle amid the ongoing RAM crisis.

During the company's FY2026 Q2 earnings call today, chief financial officer Lin Tao makes multiple references to the company's next console and its plans going forward.

"Looking ahead to next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetization through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service. We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next generation platform," she says in comments transcribed by Sony.

But that's not to say that progress isn't already being made. During the Q&A section of the earnings call – transcribed by Seeking Alpha – Tao says "we are progressing as scheduled" on research and development of the next-generation platform, reiterating: "The development itself is on schedule."

She elaborates on future plans in a later question, noting that there will be "investment for the new platform" starting in the next fiscal year and continuing beyond. "For future growth, we have to attach great importance to our new platform," she continues. "We have to make the necessary investments for that. But we have to support this soundness of our platform and try to think how rationally we can invest in our platform."

This is something that Sony will announce at an "appropriate" time in the future.

But how about those PS5 sales? Tao acknowledges that they're "gradually declining as expected in this stage of the console life cycle," but "the PS platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner."

Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+.

To get into the numbers, 2.6 million additional PS5 units were sold in the last quarter, bringing the total to 97.9 million. However, that also means it's not selling as well as the PS4 did at the same point in its lifecycle – the previous-gen console had already surpassed 100 million sales by then.

Perhaps that's unsurprising amid ongoing challenges for the PS5, though. Beyond the uproar Sony itself caused by announcing the end of physical PlayStation game production, the ongoing RAM shortage has been having a major impact on hardware prices. During the call, Tao notes that in regard to the PS5 specifically, "we have been able to offset the rise in memory prices through adjustments to promotions and pricing, as well as additional cost-reduction, and we expect hardware profitability for the current fiscal year to remain on par with the previous fiscal year."

Furthermore, she reveals: "Regarding memory procurement for next fiscal year, based on discussions held so far with various suppliers, we have aligned on the quantity of memory needed for our projected hardware unit sales."

Here's hoping, then, that we won't see any more nasty price increases for the PS5 in the months to come – let's face it, they've shot up enough as is.

Fans might not "pull out $1,000" for PS6 and Project Helix if all they can offer is marginal improvements, says ex-PlayStation boss.

#3814. Best Mitya build in Genshin Impact: Weapons, artifacts, and teams

Capable of excelling as both a meta main and sub-DPS, Mitya arrived as a godsend for all looking for an Electro Stellar-Conduct specialist in Genshin Impact.

But as he also comes with one of the most convoluted kits the game has ever produced, building him can feel like a tall task at first. Here are the best main and sub-DPS Mitya builds in Genshin Impact.

Mitya is a flexible DPS capable of dealing high on-field and off-field Electro/Stellar-Conduct DMG. The first pillar of his kit lies in his Detection Core. Generated by his Elemental Skill, the core follows and deals Electro damage to nearby enemies when in Steady State, allows Stellar-Conduct reactions to generate Gradient Beacons in Overloaded State, and provides the following:

His final Combat Passive then sets all into motion by allowing Mitya to turn all of the party’s Superconduct reactions (and their DMG) into Stellar-Conduct, now generating Gradient Beacons and putting him into Radiance. The beacons stay by the on-field character while applying the Polestar Field effect, increasing Mitya’s CRIT Rate by 5% (20% max) and boosting the team’s Stellar-Conduct DMG based on his maximum EM. Also generated via his Burst, up to four beacons can be active simultaneously.

Mitya’s signature 5-star catalyst, Starsealed Edict, is his best weapon and provides both multiple Elemental Mastery buffs and a massive amount of CRIT DMG. The latter is huge here, as Stellar-Conduct DMG can crit to maximum effect.

Following the above, Dawn­ing Frost is Mitya’s best 4-star option and can even challenge his signature if fully refined. Nefer’s Reliquary of Truth is also a perfect fit, although you won’t be able to trigger all of its passives. You can check out an overview of all weapons below:

With his recommended weapons already providing plenty of CRIT DMG, a 4-piece Disenchantment in Deep Shadow is the best option for main DPS Mitya, with a full Gilded Dreams set feeling handmade for the sub-DPS role.

All roles also demand a heavy investment in Elemental Mastery, Energy Recharge, and CRIT Rate, as you will need it to max out the team’s Stellar-Conduct DMG and his Burst uptime. Go for the following main stats to close the build:

#3813. Days Gone studio's next PlayStation exclusive to be revealed and released in 2027, according to new report

Sony's Bend Studio, perhaps one of its lesser discussed development houses, has apparently been deep in development on its next title. The game is reportedly set to be announced in 2027, and released in the same year.

That's according to MP1st, citing "people aware of what's happening at Bend". Like Days Gone, Bend's next game is in third-person. The title is said to include co-op support, but no live service elements.

The report doesn't say whether the game is based on a new IP or an existing one, but it does state that it's not a sequel to Days Gone. The game is apparently "much further along in development" than we realise, which isn't entirely surprising considering Bend has been quiet for years.

The seven years since the release of Days Gone in 2019 have been tumultuous for Bend Studio. The developer revealed in 2022 its next project is a new IP that "builds upon the open-world systems of Days Gone" and includes multiplayer elements.

Two years later, a job post described a game in development at Bend as a triple-A live service project. That unannounced game was then cancelled in 2025, triggering a wave of layoffs at the studio that took place a few months later. Bend hasn't said a word since then.

It's now clear the studio hopped on its next project following the cancellation of that live service game. Seeing as 2026 is nearly over, we're not likely to be waiting much longer to see that mysterious game unveiled.

Mckenna Grace has been working since she was a little kid, and at 20 years old, it feels like she’s done a bit of everything. She’s done drama, action, horror, romance and more, and in her next project, the book-to-screen adaptation of Sunrise on the Reaping, she’ll play out a deeply intense tragedy that also features massive action. However, while it’s clear she’s open to many kinds of projects and work, there is one thing she says no to: nudity. Surprisingly, her reasoning has to do with Disney.

As I said, when it comes to Grace's career, she's explored lots of different genres, which have put her in many different situations. I mean, in the last year alone, she’s worked on Regretting You, Five Nights at Freddy’s 2, Scream 7, PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie, The Last Kiss, Nimrods and Sunrise on the Reaping. Those are all very different movies, and during an interview with Cosmopolitan, she was asked if there are any kinds of roles she’d say no to. Here’s how she responded, and how nudity and Disney came into the conversation:

At this point, I definitely don’t do nudity or very hypersexual things. I respect anybody who can, but it’s terrifying to me. I don’t know if that’ll ever change. It’s not like I only do wholesome things—my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in Scream—but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday.

See, it’s obvious from her explanation that she has nothing against intimacy or nudity. And it seems like she has a lot of respect for actors who do work on projects that require it or very sexual sequences, like Off Campus, for example. However, it’s not her cup of tea, and I do see why.

As she said, she wants to be a Disney princess someday. If you’ve seen the best Disney movies, you know there’s a certain level of wholesomeness involved. That’s not to say an actor who participates in a project that involves sex scenes or nudity wouldn’t get a role as a Disney princess or prince. However, it’s clear Grace is trying to create an image for herself that makes her an unquestionable fit for one of these very wholesome roles.

I think she’s doing a good job at that too. I mean, before Teagan Croft and Milo Manheim were cast as Rapunzel and Flynn Rider for the live-action Tangled, Mckenna Grace and Mason Thames were popular fan casts for the parts. She legitimately looks like a princess, and her bubbly and bright personality fits right in with that kind of character too.

Now, getting back to what she said, she made it clear she’s not only going to do wholesome roles, and her work on the 2026 movie schedule clearly showcases that. I mean, Scream 7 is a horror movie, and as she said, she gets brutally murdered in it. Also, Sunrise on the Reaping is not for the faint of heart. As a fan of the book, I know how brutal the story is, and I know we’ll see Grace acting out some truly violent and intense moments.

However, while she’s willing to do work like that, she does have boundaries she does not want to cross. That means she’ll say no to projects that are hypersexual or involve nudity, which is totally respectable.

With that said, hopefully someday she’ll get her wish of being a Disney princess. While we wait for that to happen (because I do feel like it’s inevitable), you can catch Mckenna Grace in Sunrise on the Reaping on November 20.

You may well be sick of reading about it—I am certainly sick to my stomach writing about it—but here's another doom-filled prophecy about the continuing memory crisis. Doesn't seem quite so funny calling it a RAMpocalypse now. The CEO of memory module maker TeamGroup, Chen Ching, is claiming we still haven't seen the worst of the supply crisis, and that even in 2027 "there will be no downward price trend whatsoever."

According to a report from BigGo Finance, which cropped up while I was searching for a credible source after mydrivers wrote about it, Chen thinks the worst of the shortage will be from now until the middle of next year, and that we're likely to get to a point with DRAM that "even money can't buy goods".

"Right now you can still buy goods, they're just expensive," he says. "In a little while, you may not be able to buy goods at all."

This is all on the back of an earnings call for the company, where it announced record quarterly revenue of NT$10.139 billion (around $308 million), which is an increase of 34% compared with last quarter.

TeamGroup, like most memory manufacturers looking to capitalise on the current crisis, is prioritising where it can get the most cash from, and that comes from selling direct to data centre and enterprise folk, rather than us normies. Just as chatty Sam Altman would like it to be. Fully two thirds of TeamGroup's business is now selling into other businesses, where previously that percentage was just a quarter, with the majority going into the consumer market.

Chen claims its relationships with vendors will help it continue to get inventory, even if it has to pay premium spot prices for it. But he notes that supply will continue to be the big problem, suggesting that supply and demand equilibrium is unlikely to be achieved any time before the second half of 2028, or potentially even later.

And, obviously, that means prices will remain high, or more likely keep rising. "How can prices fall when there's nothing left?" he questions like a good little doom-monger. Good 'ere, innit?

#3810. Remedy revenue soars by 226% following release of Control Resonant, the developer's fastest-selling game ever

Remedy - the developer behind the recently released Control Resonant - has released a scorcher of a quarterly financial report. It shows that following Resonant's release in September, the company's revenue surged by 226 percent, bringing in €39.6m in Q3.

This performance was described as "a defining milestone for the company" by CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon. The company reported a €0.6m operating profit this quarter, a fair leap upwards from the €16.4m loss from this time last year.

There are some interesting highlights to this sudden surging performance. For one, the US made up nearly half of Control Resonant's players across PC and console, followed by Chinese-speaking regions and then the UK.

Perhaps most crucially is that nearly half of Control Resonant's players were entirely new to the franchise, with the company stating: "Reaching new players was a key goal for this game, and these early results indicate a growing audience for the franchise and for Remedy."

Control (2019) also saw a bump up in sales thanks to the release of Control Resonant, showing a stronger performance this quarter than the past two quarters this year as well as its comparison period (this quarter last year).

Remedy's CEO now believes the focus for the studio is to "get Resonant into the hands of more players." He continues to say the game has provided a solid foundation for growth as other projects (including the Max Payne 1 & 2 remake) are in the works. In short, things appear to be looking rather good for Remedy.

Control Resonant was an artistically impressive but critically divisive game. While many praised the series' adventure into third person action, some felt it had less of a narrative bite than its predecessor. Nonetheless the game quickly blasted past one million sales after launch.

Out of nowhere, GameSir announces the Nova Vision for Switch and PC players

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GameSir is probably the most prolific brand in the controller space, but as gamepads with screens have emerged from almost every corner in the last few years, GameSir has stayed silent. It's a surprise, then, that GameSir has revealed the Nova Vision today, a Switch 2 controller that's got a screen and menu system integrated into it.

Not only is it the first GameSir controller with a screen, but it's also the first with adjustable thumbstick tension. This is another emerging trend in the controller space in 2026, with FlyDigi's Vader 5S leading the charge, but being flanked by the 8BitDo Ultimate 3 and the Nacon Revolution Pro X. Usually, with this feature, you twist the thumbstick gates to either increase or decrease the physical tension in each one. On the Nova Vision, however, you twist the thumbsticks themselves.

The Nova Vision, despite its swanky new screen and innovations, will only set you back $54.99, less than the brand's GameSir G7 Pro for Xbox and PC. It'll be available in either Black or White, and has trigger stop switches as well as the other bells and whistles.

The integrated menu system, like the ones in its rival controllers, will help you adjust back button assignments, stick settings, profiles, connections, and more. It seems pretty conclusive, although it's called VisionOS - the same name as the OS used for Apple's Vision Pro headset. Hopefully that doesn't end in tears... or a lawsuit.

The Nova Vision follows on from the Nova product line, which has always been supportive of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 ecosystems. We just reviewed the Super Nova, which has become one of our go-to budget gamepad recommendations. Of course, like all Nova products, it'll also work as a PC controller.

This time around, GameSir hasn't stuck to TMR sticks, which have become the norm for all of the company's products in recent times. There are still Hall effect ones, which will prevent drift on the Nova Vision.

The Nova Vision will also feature two back buttons, although these aren't the usual individualized buttons you'll find on most GameSir products; they're the slightly longer plastic levers built into the controller's back. In my experience, these aren't quite as good, but they'll still give you a degree of extra functionality.

The Nova Vision comes with a charging stand and wireless play with a 1,000mAh battery. Like the Nova Lite, it's also broadcasting wake functionality for the Switch 2; in this instance, it's lift-to-wake, meaning that when you lift the gamepad from its stand, it'll wake the console. When we tested this feature on the Super Nova, it didn't work as advertised, so that might be one to give a wide berth.

#3807. It looks like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 had fewer active players at launch in the US compared to last year's Black Ops 7

It's been speculated for a while that Call of Duty may be losing its lustre. Although we don't have concrete data with detailed statistics for each game released in the last several years, there's an observable trend in player numbers that's hard to ignore.

US market analysis firm Circana published some data showing player engagement with Modern Warfare 4 following its launch, and compared them to those by Black Ops 7.

The data is based on Circana's proprietary Player Engagement Tracker, which tracks player activity in the US across Steam and PlayStation, and worldwide on Xbox. According to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, 19 percent of players on PlayStation played Modern Warfare 4 in the week ending 24th October, compared to 17 percent on Xbox, and 4.2 percent on Steam.

With the exception of Steam, those numbers are down compared to last year's Black Ops 7, which saw 23 percent engagement on PlayStation, 29 percent on Xbox, and a meagre 1.5 percent on Steam during its launch week.

Call of Duty managed to land in the top 10 across all three platforms during the same week ending 24th October, per Circana. In fact, it sat just below Fortnite on PlayStation, which is a decent result.

The large drop in activity on Xbox could be explained by Modern Warfare 4's lack of a day-one release on Game Pass. Black Ops 7 was the second (and last) Call of Duty to launch on Game Pass day-and-date with its premium release. Game Pass availability typically boosts player numbers, though not always sales.

The drop on PlayStation is a little harder to explain, but could be a side effect of the incredibly successful Black Ops 1 & 2 ports released in the summer on PS4 and PS5, which captured lapsed players who may have simply lost interest in modern Call of Duty, regardless of the perceived quality of Modern Warfare 4.

Judging by the data we have access to, such as SteamDB numbers showing Modern Warfare 4's launch compared to Black Ops 7's and other recent releases, there's evidence this year's game perhaps isn't as popular as it could've been.

Indeed, even Activision's tenor when talking about Call of Duty first weekend sales has changed. The publisher issued a single statement following Modern Warfare 4's launch, through Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, which does not even mention the game by name.

"One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40bn in lifetime franchise revenue," Sharma wrote on X. "An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us."

Last year's Black Ops 7 post-launch statement sidestepped talk of sales and revenue entirely, insteading praising the "great response to the quality and depth of gameplay in Black Ops 7".

Indie game storefront itch.io has expanded its AI disclosure filters, allowing its users to better separate games made with the controversial technology from those who don't.

This expansion, revealed on its official BlueSky account, includes Itchio's search page which now features a "No AI" box. By ticking this, users can hide any game on the website that features the generative AI disclosure. Games created using generative AI must have this disclosure to be present on the platform, similarly to Steam, although without an option to describe to what extent the tech was used.

This change comes shortly after itch.io also revealed the number of game pages being made on the website each day had doubled in the past two months. And, of course, the number of games downloaded and purchases have not doubled to match this new supply.

itch.io is also facing issues linked to the sheer file size. The storefront has a terms of service policy against AI spam, which it cited shortly after it publicly announced "a couple terabytes of AI slop" had been deleted.

This change comes as the industry as a whole has been clogged with an influx of AI games. Steam Next Fest had a record-breaking number of demo submissions last month. Developers pulled demos in fear of their game being copied, and with Steam saying it's the developer's responsibility to make their games less copyable.

It's an issue that isn't going away any time soon. Even as Claude creator Anthropic has introduced rules preventing unoriginal game clones, alternative AI tools can still be used to create them, and the process of creating games using AI tools will still allow for hastily made, low effort slop. Perhaps filters, like the one itch.io has expanded, is a workable solution to this on-going problem.

And it says it already knows not everyone will play nice.

Nexus Mods, the world's largest mod site and more or less a second home for anyone who's ever installed a Bethesda game, has new rules regarding AI-generated and AI-assisted mods on its platform. In short, it's taking a Steam-ish approach: no outright bans on AI content, but it's compulsory to disclose where it's been used in your mods, and to what extent.

"An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use", wrote Nexus owner Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann in an update yesterday. "We'd prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform".

So, starting yesterday, modders uploading new projects to Nexus will have to tick a box declaring how much AI was used in their work, including promotional materials. They can declare their mods "AI-generated", which is to say mostly produced by AI; "AI assisted", for mods that are mostly human-made with a little LLM assistance on the side; or declare them free of the tech's touch altogether.

"AI assisted" modders will also have to make public explanations as to where and how AI has been used, in addition to the box-ticking. The tags will be shown more prominently—right after adult-content tags.

Meanwhile, Nexus itself is pledging never to use mods to train AI or to sell them to third parties that want to do so. The site is also introducing new permissions that will let authors declare whether they are open to (non-Nexus) parties using their creations for AI use and training, with the default being "Ask Me".

How long does everyone have to get themselves in-line with the new rules? Glad you asked. "We'll also be introducing a 60-day grace period for existing mods to meet the new requirements, giving Mod Authors time to review their mods and make any necessary changes to them. This grace period starts today (3rd November 2026) and ends on 2nd January 2027."

I was a little unsure as to whether the new rules would truly apply to every mod on Nexus. There are a lot of them, after all, and plenty that have long since been abandoned by their original creators. Nevertheless, Nexus tells me that "it applies to every mod uploaded to the site, including ones that were uploaded prior to our announcement and the grace period." So better get your ducks in a row, mod authors.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Anyway, will every modder using AI dutifully hew to these rules? No, but Nexus says it knows that. "While we hope these changes will encourage everyone to disclose their AI usage, to be honest, that’s not going to happen. Additionally, we are putting clear moderation standards in place, enforced with consequences for breaking the rules", says Folmann. We'll see how it all shakes out in the months to come.

#3802. Best WoW Forever add-ons to avoid AI slop

Hey @grok, build me a World of Warcraft AI add-on. But seriously, don't.

World of Warcraft: Forever marks our return to Azeroth in the good ol’ days, and nothing says “good ol’ days” better than hopping into CurseForge to look for this month’s best add-ons. Except nowadays, World of Warcraft: Forever AI add-ons are just as common as regular ones.

And there’s usually no telling who made what. Was it a developer with an AI assistant? Maybe it’s someone and their grandma. More importantly, was it created with the same attention to detail OG devs put into their add-ons?

If it seems hastily made and just the 100th copy of something else that exists, chances are you’re dealing with AI slop. So let’s choose the best handcrafted add-ons for our new journey.

Of course, not all add-ons made with (or with the help of) AI are automatically AI slop. After all, AI tools are slowly becoming a part of professional workflows in industries like coding, with human-in-the-loop ensuring shipped products function as intended.

But this is exactly where the risk of using AI add-ons lies. Just because today’s hip model (that hasn’t gone rogue) made a “working” add-on doesn’t mean it’s 100% production-ready. At the end of the day, it’s up to each person with AI add-ons. But remember:

Players have been making WoW add-ons since 2004 (others claim since the Beta of Vanilla, so serious deja vu vibes). And many devs have been in the game for years, so they know add-ons in and out. It’s no surprise some of them already made add-ons we could use with WoW: Forever if we’re a bit nervous about AI ones:

Anyone who’s ever handled an alt knows that the go-to speed-leveling strategy is to grab as many quests as you can in an area and turn them in all at once for that sweet XP rush. But while the map already reveals where the general area of a quest is located, there’s really no in-game tool that lets you know which quests are still available in that area. That’s where Questie comes in.

This add-on enhances the map so that hovering over a zone will give you an overview of the quests you completed (and, most importantly, those that are available) in that region. There’s even a “Questie’s Journey” window that shows you a list of quests by zone and even an advanced search option.

Being a reimagined take on WoW‘s original 2004 release, it’s no surprise WoW: Forever also kept its traditional UI as part of the core experience. While Blizzard did a lot of work modernizing the UI, there’s a lot to be desired in the visuals department.

And if you’re looking for a more pleasant UI to fit the game’s updated graphics, Dialogue UI is the way to go. It adds a touch more dynamism to dialogue options, with unique looks for NPC dialogue and readables on paper and metal. You can adjust camera motion for immersion, adjust font size, copy dialogue, and even display the lore of items you pick up.

If we’re in a grinding mood, sometimes it’s a hassle to click anything other than a target on the screen. And even then, you probably set a keybind to attack a particular target. So sometimes just clicking an NPC and dialogue separately can be a hassle.

This is what DialogKey – Numy Edition wants to get us away from. Basically, it lets us bind NPC interactions to keyboard buttons. Maybe you want a one-button-fits-all option for interactions, or press a number to select a dialogue option.

The grind from Level 1 to 60 will be tougher in WoW: Forever, especially now that Blizzard wants to focus more on horizontal progression. So instead of an ever-increasing level count, we’re expecting to get side content, endgame dungeons, and other opportunities to maximize our builds.

And if you’re too busy on the grind to manually check whether it’s time to train your spells or not, then What’s Training? can make that much easier for you. It enhances the UI to let you know which spells you can upgrade now, soon-ish, and far ahead, including which levels you’d have to watch out for.

WoW has been around for more than 20 years, so naturally there are just some tiny things we wish could’ve been better. But there’s just so much Blizzard could offer in terms of settings before they become a whole host of minute details we can adjust.

On the off-chance that tinkering with hundreds of options is not a problem with you, then Enhance QoL is the add-on to get. Simply put, the add-on provides more minute adjustment options to the game’s quality-of-life features, with options for character inspection, inventory management, combat, mini-map and navigation, and more.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Not to mention, the release of WoW: Forever also comes with built-in features that we usually had to use add-ons to get. These include:

While it’s true that not all AI add-ons are slop, the disturbing number of them that are makes players uninclined to use them. Anyone can use AI to make a WoW: Forever add-on, and there’s even one that lets you make add-ons while playing the game.

Players in the “r/WoWForever” subreddit already expressed concerns about low-effort AI-coded slop add-ons throughout the beta.

You can go to the WoW: Forever page at CurseForge, sort by creation date, and you’ll see new projects pop out every few refreshes. Some honest creators include AI disclosures in the descriptions, but many don’t. Others also called out a subreddit posting trend where a user would preface “I made this add-on…” as a sign an add-on was created by AI.

“For me, it isn’t that AI made it. It’s that this person and 15 others have made slightly different variations of the exact same addon,” u/blukraken wrote in one of the posts. “How many of y’all are actually testing your addons, having another AI try to break them, looking through existing GitHub repos, or researching what other developers are doing? What would make me trust that you’d even continue iterating and fixing bugs that were found?”

In a 404 Media report, Sildri Silentcrest (Warcraft Logs CEO) told Joseph Cox that Warcraft Logs is introducing a paid commercial key, as their team noticed more users scraping their data and using their API for their own projects without credit and/or proper commercial licensing.

It doesn’t help that we’re already facing a similar crisis in game development as a whole, where a marketplace as big as Valve is littered with AI slop games while promising indie titles are hit with AI clones before they even get released.

When you get an add-on you want to use in WoW: Forever, installing it is easy. The installation process depends on how you want to approach it:

You can open the app and select World of Warcraft. Find the “WoW Forever” tab via the dropdown or by adding it from its list or scanning your computer. From there, you can see add-ons you can use. Select anything you like and click “Install.”

Find the .toc file of your add-on. Copy, cut, or move it to your local installation directory. It should be something like World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns.

From there, just open WoW: Forever, go to your options menu, and click “Add-ons.” Your recently installed add-on should be there. Enjoy!

World of Warcraft: Forever launches on November 4, 2026.

#3801. COD: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ patch has nerfed UAV Towers so you're not immediately visible everywhere you go

The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 patches continue, with the latest delivering some big changes to the game's extraction mode DMZ. The latest hotfix introduced a key balance change to one of DMZ's most controversial mechanics: UAV Towers.

UAV Towers, previously guaranteed to spawn in every Point of Interest (POI) in the map, have now had their spawn logic randomised. Infinity Ward also reduced their spawn rate by 40 percent, meaning you're less likely to find them across the various regions of the map. As noted in the patch notes, that change also prevents multiple towers from spawning the same area. The only exception is the Deadtown area, which factors into DMZ Order progression and requires multiple towers.

By taking away the guarantee that each POI will have at least one UAV Tower, the patch removes one of the core tactics PvP-inclined and aggressive players have been relying on since DMZ's launch. It's common for players to spawn in, and immediately run around activating as many UAV Towers as possible to reveal the movement of enemy players, even if they're not interested in directly engaging them.

Indeed, some of the UAV Towers cover extraction areas, so it's easy for players intending to ruin the day of others as they're extracting to set up elaborate traps. Making matters worse, a particular character trait prevents UAV Towers from expiring, allowing the scans to stay up for the entire match.

Infinity Ward has not commented directly on that trait, but the developer confirmed it's being changed so the Sedative Inhaler - which hides you from UAVs - also works with those trait-upgraded towers, though that change won't arrive until sometime in Season 1.

Finally, today's update further makes it easier to stay undetected by boosting the Sedative Inhaler's duration to 120 seconds, double that of the previous 60, which should help while we wait for larger changes to be implemented.

DMZ has been one of Modern Warfare 4's most discussed modes online. Recently, players discovered what appears to be a separate matchmaking pool for Story Missions that prevents solo sessions from featuring other players, though with some caveats.

Grey's Anatomy is one of the most legendary medical dramas of all time, and we're currently in its whopping 23rd season on ABC (and streaming with a Hulu subscription). The beloved medical drama is till going strong, but many fans like to look back at its glory days. Late actor Eric Dane famously played Mark Sloane/ McSteamy during that time, and excerpts from his posthumous memoir got honest about his struggles during that time.

McSteamy is one of the most beloved Grey's character of all time, in no small part thanks to the charisma and heart that Dane brought to the role. In his recently released memoir My Book of Days (via EW) he wrote about an injury and reliance on painkillers resulted in him deteriorating during his time at Seattle Grace Hospital. He wrote:

My body goes to shit. I drop to 170, my face caves in, my eyes cloud, I look gaunt; shit, I look like a drug addict. You can tell. I can tell. My attitude on set changes. I’m no longer bubbly, the fun guy, a ringleader in laughs. I don’t act out. I don’t throw tantrums or chairs. I go the other way. I bring everything inside. I dissolve.

What a heartbreaking recollection. While Grey's fans were still head over heels in love with Sloan, Dane was having a private struggle with his health and substances that was making his job difficult. Rather than acting out he felt himself "dissolving", and not letting it impact this coworkers. Indeed, Grey's Anatomy stars wrote tributes to the late actor following his tragic death in February.

Later in his memoir, the Euphoria star does mention that his coworkers noticed the change in him. He wrote about the dynamic he felt at the time, in a section which reads:

I can’t help it. I feel other members of the cast looking at me. They’re my friends. My work family. No. My family. They don’t judge me. They don’t look angry. They look concerned. They look sad.

It's tough to hear how Eric Dane was struggling during this time, and how he was being so private about it while bringing McSteamy to life. He didn't want to bother his co-workers and chosen family, but they noticed that something was going on. That includes the one and only Shonda Rhimes, who did offer to help the Last Ship actor. As he wrote:

I tell her I’m dealing with it. I lie to her. I lie to myself. I suck it up. Fight through it. I don’t want to be Shonda’s burden. I don’t want to be a problem. But I am. I am a problem.

Clearly Eric Dane took the time to reflect on his years on Grey's Anatomy, and the struggles he was dealing with at the time. In his book he was able to speak honestly about his issues, and take responsibility for being a "problem." It's a powerful testament, one that might help inspire readers who are dealing with similar issues.

New episodes of Grey's Anatomy air Thursdays on ABC as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Folks who want to re-watch Dane's iconic tenure as McSteamy can do so on both Hulu and Netflix. Although after hearing about his experience, it might hit differently.

#3798. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is confirmed, finally getting new trailer and full name, 8 years, 4 months, and 23 days after its reveal

Today, Xbox and Bethesda have finally revealed the name and more information about The Elder Scrolls 6. The game, which we now know carries the subtitle Sentinel, was revealed in a special video that took place today, 3rd November 2026, almost exactly 15 years since the launch of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim and eight years, four months, and 23 days since the first reveal of the title card for The Elder Scrolls 6. That's over 100 months, by the way, or 3067 days, if you want to get specific.

In the trailer, a glimpse of the new game - mostly with some fancy sand physics - before the name, Sentinel, is revealed formally. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate," says a quote in the video, attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

"For 40 years, we've explored new worlds, told unforgettable stories, and gone on incredible adventures together," says a blurb for new video. "From everyone at Bethesda Game Studios, thank you for joining us along this journey, for making these worlds your own, and for inspiring us to keep creating. Here's to 40 more."

This reveal comes after a report last week suggested we'd be seeing more of the highly-anticipated fantasy RPG in November, and which also predicted the name of the game. That report suggested that the title will take place in the Tamriel region of Hammerfell, will touch on the "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts". This trailer seems to confirm all that.

Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, said she'd played the game in August on a trip to the Bethesda offices, as a giant inflatable rat and a union protest took place outside. Notably, the reveal of the game is taking place not six months after Bethesda suffered sweeping job cuts (alongside many other Microsoft-owned studios) as part of Xbox's "reset".

So why has it taken eight years for Bethesda to show us this game? Previously, Skyrim's lead designer Bruce Nesmith noted that the studio and boss Todd Howard felt pressured to reveal the game to the world because "the pitchforks and torches were out". "[...] Todd's opinion - one which I share, by the way - is that the video game industry has short memories," he said in an interview in 2023. "Those companies that start touting their games years ahead of time, actually, you know, they screw themselves. The best time to start talking about it is six months before release." It's worth noting, then, that this is what Bethesda did with Fallout 4.

Does that hint at a timeline for more Sentinel footage being shown soon, and a potentially sooner-than-we-thought release date? Who knows. If we are going to see the game again anytime soon, it's most likely going to be during The Game Awards 2026, which is taking place on 10th December.

#3797. US midterm tsunami sweeps away video game composer who talked about ‘double booty’ and made sure to never touch anyone, just loom’

Marty O’Donnell’s bid for Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District ended in disappointment—for Marty—as he’s one of many Republican candidates who got swept away by a massive blue wave that kept Democratic incumbent Susie Lee’s seat after a 20-percent margin of victory.

You may not recognize Marty’s name, but chances are you’re familiar with his work. He served as Bungie’s main composer for over two decades, responsible for Destiny‘s soundtrack and, more importantly, Halo’s hauntingly beautiful main theme. Unfortunately, this really is a prime candidate for separating the art from the artist.

The first possibility is that Marty had received a glowing endorsement from Donald Trump shortly before the election.

It is my Great Honor to endorse America First Patriot, Marty O'Donnell, who is running to represent the incredible people of Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District. Marty is running against Susie Lee, a true Radical Left Extremist who does not represent the Values of Southern…

Unfortunately for O’Donnell, he was gunning for Nevada, a district that was greatly impacted by Trump’s unwavering stance on tariffs, so maybe that’s not the guy you want to seem very well connected to at that point. Still, there are other equally important reasons to point out, like the fact that O’Donnell is reportedly not someone you want close, or even “looming” around, especially if you’re a woman.

A few of his ex-colleagues have talked about prior experiences, none of them good. The scariest part, however, is that Marty might already be so familiar with these situations that he’s already devised a game plan.

When talking about a particularly infamous event at a Bungie Halloween party, Marty said, “Yes, the women got really creeped out but I made sure to never touch anyone, just loom.”

Oh, and that’s all after he’d become a pioneer in appropriating Halo imagery to bastardize it with AI to create anti-immigration propaganda.

After her tremendous victory, Susie Lee likely destroyed any horcruxes Marty likely still had lying around by tagging him in a tweet showing a viral video where a bunch of school kids perform a surprisingly beautiful rendition of the Halo theme inside a bathroom. The video fades to black with the message “the fight is finished.”

Enjoy your retirement @MartyTheElder pic.twitter.com/vH8KwKWrdl

I usually prefer when winners celebrate with grace and avoid teabagging their enemies, but Susie and so many others have been through so much crap because of “MartyTheElder” that I just cannot condemn anyone for double-tapping the guy.

As for Marty himself, well, he’d previously stated that he never really wanted to be a politician in the first place, so, if we’re to take his words for it, then everyone’s all the better for this result. Yes, even the people who cannot stop talking about how you shouldn’t be mixing politics with video games.

Since Patrick Stewart's death became public knowledge nearly a week ago, many across social media have been taking the time to honor the late actor. On that note, John de Lancie is now adding his voice to the many who've been sharing their memories of the Jean-Luc Picard portrayer. The beloved Q actor paid a fitting tribute to his former co-star and dropped the perfect reference tied to Picard and Q's past tussles.

While he wasn't a main character, John de Lancie's Q became one of Star Trek: The Next Generation's most memorable foes. After many adventures over the years, including Picard, De Lancie posted the following message about Stewart on Facebook:

For forty years, Q has been a thorn in Jean-Luc Picard’s side. And what a pleasure it has been to be that thorn. Patrick Stewart was a wonderful actor. He brought intelligence and depth to every role he played. It was a privilege to have worked with him. The universe is a little smaller and a little less bright today with his passing. Goodbye, Patrick. You touched so many. See you out there, Mon Capitaine.

That "mon Capitaine" brought a tear to my eye when I read it, and reminded me of some of my favorite TNG episodes. While Q and Picard's relationship ran hot and cold, I could always sense that it was always love coming from the former's end. Of course, he was certainly a jerk, putting Picard through some wtf-worthy scenarios, but I always appreciated that there was some mutual love between them at the end of Picard's second season.

I'm A Star Trek Fan, But I'd Never Heard This Cool Story About Patrick Stewart Showing Up On Jeremy Clarkson's Set

For those who haven't streamed Picard Season 2 with a Paramount+ subscription, the storyline ends with Picard's realization that Q has constructed the entire scenario he's put them through in order to help him overcome past trauma. Q then reveals to Picard that he is dying, and the two share a hug before Q sets the timeline right again.

It was emotional for me, even if it was potentially retconned when Picard Season 3 had Q return in a post-credits scene. Fans have, however, theorized that everything from the Q species exists outside of time. Therefore, his death doesn't have to be linear.

Personally, I think Q is not above faking his own death just for the thrill of pulling one over on Picard. The fact of the matter is, we'll likely never know now that Patrick Stewart is gone, though I'm sure he won't be the last to play Picard. Star Trek hasn't been afraid to recast iconic characters, though I think it'll be a challenge for someone to follow in Stewart's footsteps and play the role.

Patrick Stewart's death comes amid the celebration of Star Trek's 60th anniversary, which has been rife with bad news. As far as the franchise itself goes, there is a movie in development, but no TV shows are actively in the works as far as the general public knows. Stewart's passing certainly feels like a gut punch to the fandom and the former actors, many of whom held out hope for positive news before the year's end.

Tributes continue to pour in for Patrick Stewart, and I'm continuing to love every eulogy and story that is shared. Both Star Trek: The Next Generation and Picard are available to stream on Paramount+, so anyone who is missing the great Captain should head over there and watch some classic episodes.

He's great at hosting panels and appearing on podcasts if given the chance as well.

"I want us to have a happy ending. I want us to go out on our terms."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

New Blood Interactive has been around for more than a decade—it's celebrating its 12 year anniversary, in fact—and is still going strong. Dusk, Gloomwood, Amid Evil, Fallen Aces, Ultrakill—it's got an enviable catalogue that continues to grow. But CEO Dave Oshry is still imagining how it might end.

By keeping the studio relatively small, letting everyone work remotely, and not putting all its eggs in a franchise basket and spitting out endless sequels, it's been able to keep doing its thing. And that's the only way Oshry wants it to work.

"If we couldn't be successful doing it this way, I wouldn't want to do it at all," he tells us. "Rather than scrambling to find publisher money or investor money, I'd rather just shut it down and be like, 'We tried, we did our best, we made some cool games, that was it.' And I still want to do that. People are like, 'What's the end look like?' And I'm like, 'In 20 years, we're done. I'm gonna say goodbye, shut it down. Thanks for playing our games. That was fun. I'm gonna go fishing now.'"

Should New Blood start to struggle, Oshry has no interest in selling it to keep it alive. "I'm never gonna sell it. I'm never gonna give it to anybody else. It'll be our time." He'll be content, he says, if people remember its games fondly. "I hope people remember us like their favourite game studios from the '90s or 2000s. Except I don't want us to have the shitty ending like a lot of those studios had, where they got acquired or they went out of business. I want us to have a happy ending. I want us to go out on our terms."

It's a promise that hits a lot harder these days, with so many studios getting gobbled up and then being tossed aside. As October came to a close, EA killed off BioWare after years of mismanagement. 30 years down the drain. Like countless studios that have been acquired by the likes of EA, Microsoft and Embracer, there was no happy ending.

Oshry describes the games industry as "a machine that requires product and labour, and that's not us". Instead, he prefers to think of New Blood as a band.

"Our games are our albums. We tour, we sell merchandise, and everybody plays their part. We're like an orchestra now, actually, more than a band. Because we got a lot of people, and a lot of musically inclined people. We're like the Trans-Siberian Orchestra at this point.

"Eventually the band's gonna get old, and we're gonna get tired, and we're gonna do our retirement tour, and we're gonna call it a day before we get sad. Before we're on stage and people are like, 'Ah, they're getting a little long in the tooth. They can't hit those high notes anymore.' So before that happens, I want to shut it down and enjoy my life."

#3793. Square Enix will ‘most likely’ focus on new games after Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, producer says

What's next? Will the fantasy finally be final?

Mainline Final Fantasy entries have taken a bit of a backseat in lieu of the FF7 remake trilogy, but that should be changing soon.

The trilogy’s producer Yoshinori Kitase teased the franchise’s future in a new interview, but I also wouldn’t hold my breath for Final Fantasy 17 launching any time soon after FF7 Revelation drops this April.

“I think that mainly we are more likely to invest in new titles and new games, but at the same time, for example, this time with the [FF7] remake, there was me and other creators who worked on the original game, which we had really strong feelings towards,” Kitase said when asked about new IP and remakes in the interview with IGN. “And we really wanted to create something new related to the old game to allow new users to play and to know the appeal of this game as much as the old users who play the old game. So there might be different cases like this one where the company is willing to invest in remaking old projects and other kinds of games like it happened this time.”

That’s…not really a definitive answer either way regarding remakes vs. new entries vs. new IP at Square, which is notoriously busy with multiple RPG releases year in and out across its numerous dev teams. For example, this year alone, the company has released Final Fantasy Resonance, The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales, Bravely Default Flying Fairy HD Remaster, and a few others.

Kitase’s words are iffy no matter how you look at it, but mainline FF entries have generally slowed down quite a bit. FF16 launched in 2023, but FF15 released way back in 2016. Meanwhile, FF7 trilogy games have come out in 2020, 2024, and next year again in 2027.

I’m generally a very big fan of the remake trilogy, and FF7 Revelation is one of my most anticipated titles of 2027, but I have a hard time imagining the company going on to remake another game… although I would not be against it, for several classic titles (6, 8, 9, or 10, please). Additionally, this year, FF Resonance has shown a true thirst and appreciation for classic turn-based games on top of the action-combat focus of recent titles, so I’ll be heavily tuned in to see what direction the series goes next.

Check out the full IGN interview for more from Kitase, including his thoughts on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 being heavily inspired by Final Fantasy classics.

It’s been a big year for Kelly Clarkson, one marked by considerable change for her. Back in August, viewers were treated to the final episode of The Kelly Clarkson Show, which wrapped up the talk show’s seven-season run. Clarkson has since partaken in other ventures, like returning to her coaching duties on The Voice. That aside, October proved to be a long month for her due to that controversy involving the mechanical bird. Now, though, I’m hoping Clarkson is celebrating some major news regarding her since-ended show.

Last week, the 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards were held, where various stars took home the coveted golden trophies for their work on the small screen. Clarkson’s eponymous chat show was among the programs in the mix, as it was nominated in 11 categories (which ensured it would go out with a bang). The show ultimately proved to have a great outing at this year’s ceremony, as it ended up winning five awards. Check out the specific categories below:

In snagging those five categories, the series managed to edge out long-running soap opera General Hospital, which took home four awards. As it stands, Kelly Clarkson’s show now has a total of 27 Daytime Emmys, which is incredibly impressive. It’s impressive to look at that from the larger perspective of the show’s run but, more immediately, it’s sweet to see the show bow out with several additional statues under its belt. The Outstanding Daytime Talk Series award is particularly impressive.

This award-heavy development is a stark contrast to the viral situation that Clarkson has been involved with over the past month. In recent weeks, the entertainer has been involved in a beef of sorts involving a novelty store, and it remains a topic of public discussion.

The $15,000 (Or $15 Million Bird) Is Way, Way In Demand After Kelly Clarkson Drama

In October, Clarkson took to social media to post about an experience she apparently had at Art of Play, a store located in Brooklyn. Clarkson claimed she’d been treated like Julia Roberts’ character from Pretty Woman, as she was apparently wanting to purchase a singing bird automaton. The store’s management team later responded to the claims, saying that they tried to explain to Clarkson that the bird was not for sale and used exclusively for in-store events. However, Clarkson seemed to counter that notion when she shared a photo of the bird with a $15,000 price tag.

Further updates have since cropped up regarding this situation, with the store’s security footage even being leaked by journalist Pablo Torre. AoP, which is owned by children' s book author Adam Rubin, has reportedly received backlash on social media, and patrons of the establishment have as well. While Clarkson allegedly believes she’s not at fault in the matter, insiders claim that those in her inner circle have been surprised by how this situation has escalated.

As of right now, it’s unclear whether or not Kelly Clarkson and Art of Play will come to any kind of understanding. In the meantime, though, Clarkson can celebrate her talk show being honored with a few more Emmys following its successful run.

#3791. Arc Raiders devs say that using generative AI voice acting was necessary as actors "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

CCO states: "We are not in the industry of replacing actors.".

Developers at Embark Studios, the company behind Arc Raiders, have spoken on the use of generative AI voice acting in the extraction shooter. It's argued that the initial use of generative AI line reads was a benefit to the voice actors, as they: "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that".

This comes from a recently released video by Embark, focused on Arc Raider's sound and music. In it, several key members of staff speak on the game's use of generative AI, be it the initial use of it for voice lines, and the gradual replacement of it with human line reads.

Audio director Bence Pajor first spoke about the struggles he ran into at previous studios; how gameplay decisions couldn't be changed because voice lines were already locked in. He describes this as a "true pain", and that it places stress on the writing team, dialogue team, and voice actors who may have scheduling clashes. He said that using reachable voice actors in Stockholm, and using the tools available, made life easier for everyone.

Later in the video, Pajor explained that training data was made with the voice actor's performances. Due to the voice lines being required for each new feature, item, or weapon added into the game, he argues it would be too impractical to record every possible version of a line read. "The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that," Pajor said.

Pajor continues by pointing to Arc Raider's many updates and changes since its release in October 2025, it would be impractical to call in voice actors to record lines every time an altered line read needed to happen. Two voice actors present in the video - Jo Rideout (Shani) and Diana Gardner (Celeste) - also shared their feelings on it. Gardner said it was "freeing" that she could take a job somewhere else, without worrying about cancelling other shoots or projects.

However, Gardner would later speak on the topic of her ownership of Celeste's many lines in the game: "The contract seemed so fair [...] so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' [...] This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Even with these proposed benefits to using AI-powered performances, these voice lines are being replaced. Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg said: "we are not in the industry of replacing voice actors", and acknowledges that immersion-breaking experiences many players had when playing Arc Raiders and hearing these performances. Strandberg and Pajor both admit to understanding the AI critique, and point to the work being done to replace what they can.

"We are not in the industry of replacing actors," said Strandberg. "Actually I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance and give them more space. That's something I'm hoping to give to players over the coming years."

Part of this critique over generative AI's use in Arc Raiders came from reviews, including our own. Embark Studios faced similar pushback for gen-AI voice acting in The Finals, however Arc Raider's popularity while using the technology led Nexon to describe it as a "trojan horse" for gen AI's use in small team game development.

#3790. Country of Fortune release countdown: Exact date and time

Country of Fortune is coming soon to gamers worldwide, and less than 24 hours are left for it to go live. Developed by Nepos Games, Country of Fortune takes city-building to a new level. Instead of constructing your city, you’ll be developing an entire nation, and every decision you make will have a key impact on your legacy.

But first, let’s find out when the upcoming nation-builder goes live.

Country of Fortune goes live worldwide on Thursday, November 5. The release date was announced by the developers earlier, and I am not expecting any change this late. The following countdown will expire once the game goes live.

The countdown is based on the following times.

If there is any change to the schedule ahead of launch, I will duly update it on this guide.

In Country of Fortune, you build an entire medieval country with the use of your settlements. The game uses grids, grows, and knits into a living region filled with people, rivers, and resources.

As a lokator, your first task is to pick a suitable grid to place your first settlement. Then, guide all your villages to help them grow from a hamlet to a bustling city.

Since no two grids are the same, you’ll need to adjust accordingly. There will be plenty of resource deposits to exploit, but you’ll be challenged by the environment and terrain.

With a wide economy, you’ll need to manage plenty of different aspects. Develop settlements and help them specialize in producing goods that require resources from the nearby areas. You can also develop roads and vehicles to set up a booming trade.

With different levels of power and endless micromanagement (if you want), Country of Fortune has plenty of exciting features to offer. If you’re unsure about what to expect, there’s a free demo available on Steam for you to try out ahead of the game’s early access launch.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

We are back. After a long sojourn to the centre of the self, I return—having completed a journey of discovery where I reflected on what I really wanted from modding GTA 5: my true desires, true capabilities, and where I want to take this whole thing as we walk, together, into the future. I speak to you now of the wisdom I have gained from my vagabond travels, behold:

I've put roving packs of hostile cougars in the game now.

The mod to put loads of cougars in Grand Theft Auto 5 is called Cougars, which is easy to remember, and it boasts "seven special cougar types" and four difficulties. Cougar time is initiated with a tap of the delete key, at which point you may choose either Catnap, Furmidable, Feral, or Catastrophe mode, which I am led to believe affects the volume of the cat hordes dispatched against you and the potency of their armaments.

Naturally, I opted for Catastrophe, kicking off a sort of pseudo-game-show opening where Franklin, Trevor, Michael, and Franklin's celebrity bodyguard were all fleeing angry litters of cats. Then we were off, with me—as Franklin—desperately dodging leaping cougars, some of them armed with heavy machine guns, some wearing body armour, some with traffic cones for reasons known only to God. Then I teleported, and the cougars followed me.

This process continued for a few minutes before I realised that, most likely, I was not going to reach my goal of a private jet waiting on the runway at Los Santos International. I performed a rare purposeful teleport to bring myself home, at which point about 56 quintillion cougars attempted to kill me. I solved this problem with an explosive micro-SMG.

When I boarded the plane, I was told I had won, and a man with a cougar for a head and a parade of dancing regular cougars behind him all congratulated me. I teleported away in the middle of their performance. It is good to be back.

#3788. The Dark Souls Devs Are Masters At Looney Tunes–Style Physical Comedy

I used to think that Dark Souls was a very serious game. A serious, serious game for serious, hardcore gamers. Grimdark, full of esoteric mysteries and depressing, philosophical themes. Tragedy in every sense. No hope for its characters. Any shred of light snuffed out by the encroaching shadow.

I have been delighted to learn in more recent years that this is actually wrong, and Dark Souls (and its sequels, both real and spiritual) are actually comedy games. Dark Souls is video-game Looney Tunes.

— Rebekah Valentine (@duckvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-10-30T04:27:18.287Z

What the fuck is that?! A skeleton attached to a wheel of bones? A bonewheel? I guess?!

Yeah, that’s some of the funniest shit I’ve ever seen. It’s basically just this:

A lot of games try really hard to be funny via attempts at witty writing or quippy characters. Some succeed, some fail. But with Dark Souls (and Elden Ring, which I played a few years ago), FromSoftware proves it is is superb at something I imagine must be incredibly difficult to do in video games: physical comedy. You have to take into account player movement, enemy AI, objects getting caught on one anotherâthe delicate dance required to make a physical gag happen in a game like this takes such an expert hand. And yet, FromSoftware manages to Wile E. Coyote the player into incredible slapstick moments over and over, through clever use of environmental hazards and very smart enemy placement within them. You can’t tell me that reaching a tight corner and looking carefully around it just to see this sort of bullshit isn’t funny:

— Rebekah Valentine (@duckvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-11-01T03:17:26.196Z

Yes, many (most) of these scenarios result in player death, which can be frustrating, but how can I be mad at dying if my death was absolutely hilarious? How can anyone at all be mad when your death animation looks this stupid?

— Rebekah Valentine (@duckvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T01:47:56.059Z

It’s even better when it’s self-inflicted, which it so often is.
