With the Xbox Series X and S rapidly ageing, it looks unlikely that the next console generation will be affordable at all. As such, I've been looking at AMD to bring its modern GPU feature set to older hardware to stop me from having to upgrade. It seems it felt my gaze, and Xbox Series X, S, and Xbox handhelds now have FSR 4.1.2 support, which developers can turn on in their games.

AMD has just updated its Game Development Kit with FSR 4.1.2 and two new upscaling models for Xbox Series X and S: the Full INT8 model and the more efficient Lite INT8 model. The Lite one is half the size of the Full one and has a lower upscaling cost. Either console can use either model, but game developers are able to choose which type they implement.

AMD has put out a GDK sample for developers to test, which "switches between the Full and Lite models at runtime, so developers can compare image quality and upscaling cost in the same scene. Upscaler memory is the same for both models because it depends on render and display resolution, not on the model. That makes the choice a performance trade-off, not a memory one."

Interestingly, Ancient Gameplays tested the Lite and Full models two weeks ago and noticed that Lite works better with lower input resolution and even removes some visual noise that is kept in the Full model. They say the "Lite model needs to be more stable because it will be aimed at handheld devices, iGPUs from laptops, and the render resolution on those cases will be way, way lower."

FSR 4.1.2 is also now supported on Xbox handhelds (the top-end ROG Xbox Ally range to start with), though this is seemingly only the one "highly efficient INT8 model", and developers can only get access via Asus' preview driver for the Xbox Ally X and X20. AMD says "it upgrades DirectX 12 games with FSR 3.1 or newer, and ROG Xbox Ally support follows in a later update."

How developers choose to integrate FSR 4.1.2 on Xbox Series X and S will be on a case-by-case basis, but the Lite model being solid certainly suggests good things for future optimisations. And RX 6000 graphics cards got FSR 4.1 early, just a few weeks ago, giving older hardware a little bit more performance.

This is all just in time for a huge launch on Xbox: Grand Theft Auto 6. The game officially launches on November 19, and being a Rockstar game, it's looking like it will be a real graphical showcase. But playing on six-year-old hardware could pose a challenge, so getting an upscaling hand just before the game reaches the starting line surely can't hurt its reception. You won't be able to play the game on Xbox handhelds until the PC port (they aren't really Xbox consoles after all), but I won't be complaining when I'm squeezing a bit more performance out of my Z2 Extreme chip in everything else.

As first reported by South Korean news outlet INVEN (via Automaton Media), compromises to the gameâs client occurred on September 27 when hackers were able to inject malicious code inside of four JavaScript files on Level Infiniteâs online servers. #3720. Why the Holidays Are Actually the Best Time of Year to Start Working Out

If you have even the tiniest inkling that you might want to get in shape in the new year—or anytime really—don’t wait until January. This isn't a "winter arc" self-improvement pitch; it's just facts. The best time to start a gym habit is before the holiday season. Heck, in December, you’ll even have the place mostly to yourself.

Sure, technically “right now” is always the best time to start exercising, but the holiday season is special. If you wait until January, gyms will be packed. The first two weeks of the year, everybody thinks they’re at the start of an amazing new fitness habit...and by February, most of them have forgotten all about it. Don’t make life harder for yourself by starting during the big rush. Classes will fill up, you’ll have to fight people for the squat rack, and it will be hard to have any real fun. So start now.

In October and November, gyms and classes are at more or less their normal capacities. This is a good time to feel out the vibe of a new place. But it gets better: Once December rolls around, the fair-weather gymgoers will be off shopping for gifts after work and attending holiday parties on the weekends. They won’t feel like getting out of their warm beds in the morning, either. When you arrive, the squat rack will be free. You’ll have your choice of treadmills. The gym will be your oyster.

If you start now, you'll have about two months to get up to speed before the rush starts in January. And that is a perfect little time frame to set a small goal and keep it. Vow to hit the gym three times a week, and you’ll be able to get in 24 workouts before Christmas, even if you take a few days off for festivities. You can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Or run, if that's the fitness journey you're most excited about. If you start a couch-to-5k running plan now, you’ll be routinely running 30 minutes at a stretch by the time we get to January.

Yes, the holiday season can be busy and stressful, but remember that working out tends to help our brains manage stress. Mark workouts on your calendar, and keep those appointments with yourself.

Don’t worry about missing out on deals. Any gym or studio that offers a January special probably offers sales year-round anyway. And ultimately, if you get into the habit of actually using the gym, you're getting a lot more value for your money than somebody who joins in January and quickly stops showing up.

Nintendoâs total âunit sales of softwareâ saw a healthy increase in Q1-Q2 2027, with Switch 2 software sales up 18.8 percent on 2025 and Switch software sales up 6.8 percent. There are some surprise hits on the software front, with Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream shipping an enormous 8.81 million units and Rhythm Heaven Groove hitting 2.89 million units across the six-month period.

However, Nintendoâs report states that âthe continued weakness of the yenâ has led to overall sales in its âdedicated video game platform businessâ declining by 15.3 percent year-on-year. Likewise, both Bloomberg and Reuters note that Nintendoâs operating profit fell by 16 percent in its second fiscal quarter, although this was a figure Nintendo had been expecting.

Although Bloombergâs report states that Nintendoâs âbigger-than-expected 15 percent decline in salesâ is a cause for concern, with Morningstarâs equity analyst saying that it is proof that âinvestors have cooled on the Switch 2 platform,â the companyâs shares remain steadfast. In fact, as of writing, Nintendo Co Ltdâs share price is up 6.3 percent following its quarterly earnings report.

This may partially be due to a strong gross profit report, up 22.1 percent in FY2027 Q1-Q2 versus the year before. Nintendoâs report partially attributes this to both its âsolid software salesâ and the ârefunds of U.S. tariffs imposed under IEEPA that had previously been recorded as cost of sales.â

It’s important to note that while analysts believe Grand Theft Auto VIâs lack of release on Nintendo Switch platforms will make a sizable dent in the companyâs profits across the Christmas period, Nintendoâs Q1-Q2 2027 report does not include the software sales of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

Intel has promised to do it itself, but Linux devs are an impatient bunch.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Intel has already committed to bringing its XMX-powered upscaling and frame generation tech to Linux via Valve's Proton compatibility layer, but one enterprising developer is clearly not willing to wait for the chip behemoth to get it working and has released an experimental version on Github (via Phoronix).

This new release promises "real Intel XeSS super resolution and XeSS Frame Generation inside Proton games, running on the GPU's XMX (matrix) units instead of the DP4a fallback that stock Wine/Proton gets." It was built on a OneXPlayer 3 handheld running the same Intel G3 Extreme chip that ships in the latest MSI Claw and the new Acer Predator Atlas 8, but has also been tested on a discrete Arc B580 GPU, too.

And it's already delivering a 29% performance boost in Cyberpunk just from the switch to XMX processing of upscaling, and when you throw in XeSS Frame Generation you're looking at a 145% performance boost. That is just one game, however, and the only other benchmark they note is for Forza Horizon 6 where the performance boosts are not quite so great, with a 16% bump from the XMX implementation. Though again you are looking at a healthy frame rate increase from 3x frame generation.

The installation seems surprisingly straightforward; you just unpack the release archive somewhere safe and run the install command. Then every game will run with the patched drivers without the need for any special launch options.

The one note is that you must be running the native Steam client to support the XMX switch in Proton, with the Flatpak Steam client not being currently supported.

It's great to see this being picked up and running with Intel's Arc GPUs right now. The ideal would be to have Intel get the official release out and available for anyone running SteamOS, or any other Linux distro, with their Arc-based graphics silicon, but given how straightforward this implementation seems to be, it's a great stop gap measure.

And it's worth noting that while graphics card prices have become an apocalyptic nightmare, where you might have to barter a kidney or two just for the privilege of potentially buying an RTX 5060, the two Intel Battlemage cards are still relatively affordable. The Arc B580 is around $330 and the Arc B570 is a shade over $300 today. That makes them solid 'budget' cards, and now they're becoming great options for that little Linux gaming tower you always wanted to build, too.

Let me just go in on the state of the tag team division real quick.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

You might have to go all the way back to WrestleMania VII to find a WWE premium live event with so much uncertainty and venue drama ahead of the event. At this point, it appears we are moving ahead with holding Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia, but it will not take place at the original outdoor venue in Riyadh because of security concerns. Instead, it’ll take place inside the ANB Arena and will feature four matches, all of which include very top tier talent.

Now, whether they’re the most exciting matches in the world, however, is another matter entirely. It kind of depends on whether you care about long-term booking. The concept of Crown Jewel is that it brings together the world champions on both the men’s and women’s sides to compete in what’s essentially a who’s better match. The result doesn’t typically have any long-term repercussions. It’s just a showcase for the biggest names in WWE to compete, which is both fun and largely toothless.

This year, we’re getting a card that includes showcase matches featuring Roman Reigns vs Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan vs Chelsea Green. Neither has been built like a WrestleMania main event, but there’s definitely some intrigue and fun to be had in each. We’re also getting a tag team championship match featuring The Vision and the latest round of the Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes feud that feels like it’s been going on for ten years. Before I get into what I think is going to happen though, you can check out my prediction record for the biggest WWE events so far this year, as well as my overall success for every PLE since WrestleMania 38.

Cody Rhodes defeated Randy Orton during the main event of night one at WrestleMania 42 in the midst of the very divisive Pat McAfee storyline. Orton then got his revenge on Rhodes at Saturday Night’s Main Event back in September. Now we’re getting a third match, and the story they’re telling is pretty clear. In order to beat Orton, Rhodes is going to need to go to a much darker place than normal and probably punt the Viper’s head to win the match. It’s not the sort of thing a traditional good guy would do, but everyone involved seems to feel Cody needs a bit of a spark and new direction after four years of being a mid 90s Bret Hart style babyface.

The crowd still loves Rhodes and Orton, but I don’t think anyone is looking for the feud to continue after this match. That’s why Rhodes is almost certainly going to win. We’ve done this dance about whether he’s going to get more heelish and evil for much of his title run, and either it needs to happen or not. We can’t just keep teasing it. He needs to punt Orton in the head and then we need to see the fallout of what that means for his character.

It’s no secret that WWE’s tag team division is an absolute mess right now, and nothing symbolizes the company’s failing multi-year strategy more than this match. No one involved here is a tag team wrestler or even wrestles tag team matches on a regular basis. Breakker and Theory just hold the belts because it’s a cheap way to give The Vision some level of credibility since they don’t have any of the major titles. It’s the same thing we’ve repeatedly seen with The Judgment Day and other lower main event performers who need something to do.

As someone who loves tag team wrestling, matches like this are uniquely frustrating. That’s not to say the actual in-ring work will be bad. Everyone involved here is very capable and will put on a terrific show, but the whole exercise is basically pointless when we know Penta is way more concerned about cashing in his Money In The Bank briefcase, and Bron is way more concerned about finally winning his first world championship. This is just something for each of them to do because Triple H and company aren’t ready to pull the trigger in the main event scene.

I think The Vision is probably going to retain here because it just feels like The World Tag Team Championships would get in the way for Penta, but ultimately, it doesn’t really matter because no one involved in this match even aspires to be a tag team champion.

The real story here is whether Tiffany Stratton is going to cash in her Money In The Bank briefcase during this match. She’s been repeatedly teasing pulling the trigger on Liv Morgan since she shockingly beat Roxanne Perez in the stipulation match, but many fans, myself included, think she’s going to eventually cash in on her BFF Chelsea Green instead. That’s a much better long-term storyline and will allow Stratton to take her character in a more exciting direction since she’s been kind of stuck in the mud.

If Tiffy Time doesn’t get involved in this match, Liv Morgan should win. I’m not saying she’s for sure going to win, but if WWE cares anything at all about logic, she should win. Morgan is one of WWE’s strongest in-ring female performers, and while Chelsea Green is fine enough in the ring, there’s been a lot of fan talk about how sloppy and slow some of her recent matches have been. That’s not entirely been her fault, but she’s still been a part of some bad in-ring work. The whole point of Crown Jewel is supposed to be for fans to get a dream match where we get to see who would win what’s essentially an in-ring technical contest. That’s clearly Morgan.

I think there’s a high likelihood this match ends up with a bunch of shenanigans and maybe a cash-in. If it’s just a straight up wrestling contest though, Morgan should clearly win.

The only thing that matters in this match is whether the 946 interfere in it. WWE is not going to let Sami Zayn beat Roman Reigns in a straight up match, and even if they were open to the possibility, it wouldn’t make sense for their characters. Roman is repeatedly depicted as a dominant champion who is now winning matches without his family’s help. Zayn is repeatedly shown hanging on to his WWE Championship by desperate, narrow margins. A loss wouldn’t really hurt him, whereas with Roman, it would cost him some real aura points and chip away at his character.

My guess is they’re not going to interfere. We have seen a clear effort from WWE over the past year or two to keep all the shenanigans and outside noise away from Roman’s matches. The goal of almost all of them has simply been to put on a banger and prove Reigns is a fantastic in-ring worker and not just a visually-appealing package with a good entrance and strong catch phrases. I think that trend continues here, and I think he gets the best of Zayn in a competitive but ultimately clean match that Roman wins.

Desmond and Kristy share two sons: Vance and Westin.)

Desmond broke his silence later that same day when he admitted via Instagram that he’d made “choices that I am not proud of” while working through the split.

“I want to begin by apologizing to Kristy, our family, and everyone who has been impacted by the public attention surrounding this situation,” Desmond wrote via his Instagram Story. “I know this news has been disappointing for many, and I’m truly sorry for the hurt it has caused.”

He continued, “Kristy is the mother of my children, and that will always come first. I remain fully committed to being an active, present, and loving parent to our boys, as I have always been.”

Kristy and Desmond met when they were teenagers and got married in 2014. Although they frequently appeared on each other’s social media over the years, Kristy last posted content with Desmond in December 2025.

I had some health issues last year, and I was going through a lot of things personally,” Bensimon confided in her listeners. “It really made me see what I wanted in my romantic life, and how I wanted to navigate that and move forward into 2026.”

#3715. I Tested ChatGPT's New 'Slides' Tool, and Here's How It Compares to Gemini

David Nield is a technology journalist from Manchester in the U.K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years.

He has a bachelor's degree in English Literature from Durham University, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper Palatinate. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U.K. and internationally. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.

ChatGPT's capabilities continue to expand apace, and the latest feature is a fully capable slideshow creator. Announced a few weeks ago, ChatGPT Slides lets you create PowerPoint-style decks from inside your conversations, and it's now appearing for those on the Pro tier and above (meaning right now, you need to spend at least $100 a month to get it).

If you're on the free ChatGPT plan or the $20-a-month Plus tier, you can still get ChatGPT to generate downloadable PowerPoint files from the content of your conversations. However, they'll be more basic than those made in the full version of ChatGPT Slides, and there are no collaboration or native edit options.

ChatGPT Slides is part of OpenAI's push to give users a complete office suite inside the ChatGPT apps. Pages (the word processor) is already available for Pro tiers and above, while a spreadsheet app is on the way—the idea being that you will soon be able to get all your work done without any help from Google or Microsoft.

While Chatgpt Slides is only available on pricey plans right now, it's likely to come to lower subscription tiers in the future. But for now, how does the tool compare to what's available in the free and Plus tiers, not to mention what you can do with Gemini inside Google Slides? I've taken a detailed look.

When it comes to testing out AI tools, it helps to focus on something you're already knowledgeable about so you can spot any mistakes. To test this, I decided to see what ChatGPT could hoover up from the web about the new iPhone Duo. If you're on the free or Plus plans, you can start a conversation, then ask for a slideshow or PowerPoint about it.

Plus accounts also have access to a specific Presentations add-on, available via the + (plus) menu in the prompt box, though I get the impression this feature is in a state of flux since ChatGPT Slides arrived. In any case, you can begin asking about the iPhone Duo specs and early online reactions, and then say "build me a slideshow on the key features and reviews so far".

What I got back on the $20 Plus account was a fairly competent slideshow on Apple's foldable, with accurate information as far as I could see, and a simple series of layouts. It looked like something you might whip up from a template if you were in a rush and didn't have time to properly align all the bullet points or be very selective about which details you included and which you left out. One neat touch is that ChatGPT was able to drop in an official photo of the iPhone Duo at the start of the slideshow, but I had to specifically ask for one.

You can go back and make specific edits to the slideshow, but you have to describe them in the general prompt box—you can't select individual slide elements and make more precise changes. Still, if all you want to do is occasionally convert your ChatGPT conversations into a rough and ready slideshow, there's no real need to upgrade from the free or Plus accounts for now.

Switching to a Pro account, I gave a similar task to ChatGPT Slides hoping for something more comprehensive. To begin with, Slides gets its own dedicated area in the app, so you can start up a blank presentation from scratch—there are some basic image and text features, but the idea is to use prompts to build your slide deck. It's like a really basic Google Slides, with a prompt box.

Creating a slideshow this way feels rather tedious: Typing out what you want to say and then waiting for ChatGPT to do it isn't as intuitive as just throwing in some graphics and text yourself, as you might do in PowerPoint. It also seems to be a bit buggy, at least during the time I spent testing it, with some requests not properly completing.

Starting a standard conversation with ChatGPT and then turning all the information into a deck is much more useful from my perspective. My iPhone Duo slideshow was longer, laid out better, and more informative than the one I created on the Plus plan—there were even charts of battery life and official photos this time.

However, whether I used the free, Plus, or Pro tools, my presentations didn't come across as particularly well thought through. They don't really flow smoothly, either across individual slides or the slideshow as a whole—it feels very much like an algorithm, rather than a person, has decided what information to include and where on the slides to stick it.

Whether you create presentations in chats or through the ChatGPT Slides space, you're able to click on individual elements and do some basic manual resizing and repositioning. You can also request edits via prompts: "Drop in an image of a cat", "make this pop more", "center all of this information", or whatever it is.

ChatGPT Slides does offer collaborative tools, which I wasn't able to test, and I can see that being useful for teams heavily invested in ChatGPT's ecosystem. I can also imagine ChatGPT Slides coming in handy when you've got a lot of information you need to quickly dump into a slideshow that looks vaguely presentable.

In general though, I think I'd much rather stick to the traditional way of making slideshows for now. These old methods are more precise and more manageable, and give you full control over what's shown and where—even if they do take a bit longer. What's more, modern-day presentation tools come with so many templates and other layout aids that it's not difficult to put together something that's easy on the eyes while including all of the information you think is most critical.

Google is, of course, also all the way in on AI (and then some), and if you pay for Google AI Pro ($19.99 a month) or above, you can have Gemini pop up right inside Google Slides to give you some assistance with your presentation-making. To compare the tools, I gave it the same task as I did ChatGPT, asking for a slide deck on the new iPhone Duo.

Gemini actually asked some questions along the way: about wht visual style to use, the audience to aim the slideshow at, and the details to highlight. Though it's always possible to put this sort of information manually into a prompt, this would be a helpful additional to ChatGPT Slides.

What Gemini and Google Slides produced was impressive in terms of the layout and overall vibe of the presentation: It felt much more like a human being had put together the slide deck compared to what ChatGPT had produced, in terms of the information chosen, the way the slides were laid out, and the color picks.

However, Google's result had its faults too: The presentation got the facts on the maximum brightness of the iPhone Duo screen wrong, and produced an "iPhone Duo" graphic that looked like two iPhones from around 2021 stuck together. ChatGPT Slides at least managed to pull official imagery from the Apple website.

You can't attach individual edit prompts to specific parts of your presentation in Google Slides as you can in ChatGPT Slides—you have to mention them in the general prompt box. That said, Google Slides is obviously a much more mature and established slideshow tool compared to the OpenAI equivalent, in terms of its features and layout options (it has been around for a decade, after all).

Given that extra software structure and the lower cost of entry, Gemini and Google Slides is the better option for AI-assisted slideshow making at the moment—though I wouldn't bet against OpenAI catching up. For now, ChatGPT Slides is something that's good to have available if you're already paying a lot for ChatGPT every month, but not a feature that makes it worth your while to swap your AI allegiance.

I did not expect the season of Nobody Wants This that aired on the 2026 TV schedule to change my feelings about Morgan and Sasha, but it did. While I’m still not on board with them being endgame, I do see the vision of them as a couple, and I’m not mad about it. However, I do still feel weird about them, and I’m happy Justine Lupe does too.

Justine Lupe, who plays Morgan, has been open in the past about not being totally on board with her character and Sasha making things romantic. In fact, in early 2025, she said she thought there was fun to be had with them being “weird friends,” while them acting on their romantic feelings could destroy a family and that’s “not fun.”

However, everything changed in Season 3 of Nobody Wants This, as Sasha and Esther broke up and started seeing other people. A door opened for Timothy Simons and Lupe’s characters, and they walked through it in New York City. While the Morgan actress was here for it, she did note how weird it was to film on Armchair Expert, explaining:

When we were filming the kiss that we had, every time Tim and I would kiss, I’d have this freak-out. I would just like giggle, and in one of the takes I even cut us.

Then, through laughter, Simons emphasized that his co-star was the one to call cut…not the director. The Succession actress then said this happened as they were making out and going to bed, and eventually she just had to yell cut. According to the Veep actor, this all was odd for them, partially because they’re “such close friends” in real life. Lupe confirmed that, and further explained why this whole situation was odd for her:

Well, this is what it was. It was that we are very, very close friends, like brother/sister, and it was confronting to have Tim present such sex appeal. I was like, ‘You put me on the back foot.’ Like, it actually got me flustered. I was like, ‘Oh my god, ' 'cause he comes in so hot, and it was kind of disorienting.

While Morgan and Sasha’s relationship has always bordered on romantic and their chemistry is undeniable, it never really got there until this season. And it was a bit odd when it did. Their siblings are dating (and now they’re married), so in my head, they’ve always just been close friends and kind of like siblings. OK, maybe that’s me manifesting what I want for them more than anything; however, the point is: I have a hard time picturing them being romantic.

Clearly, the actors kind of felt that way too, but not in a bad way. Explaining that further, Lupe said:

I got giddy and weird about it, because I was like, ‘Oh my god, my buddy is getting all hot on me.’

“Giddy and weird” is the perfect way to describe my feelings about Sasha and Morgan hooking up. For the longest time, this happening was my biggest Nobody Wants This fear. However, the way it happened on the show was so compelling, dramatic and sincere that I couldn’t help but be happy about it.

As Simons noted, this whole situation felt “earned” and “organic,” which I totally agree with. If Morgan and Sasha were going to get together, this was the way to do it, and I’m so happy the actors who play them understand both how odd and lovely this whole situation is.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular—and while I was preparing for the launch last night, I was bracing for the same experience I had in the beta. Namely: Long queue times, connection errors, and disconnects. At least I wouldn't have to use a VPN this time, I thought, that is some small saving grace.

Turns out I needn't have worried. There was a brief panic, mind, when I finished a breezy five minute queue and landed on a ruleset selection screen that was completely greyed-out. But one eight minute queue later, and I was in—and proceeded to quest until 4 am with nary a disconnection or lagspike to be seen.

Granted, I am playing on both the EU realms and the roleplay ruleset, both of which are bound to be less populous. But having hopped online, it doesn't seem like I'm alone: "I fully expected to not be able to play today, but I logged in with no queue and no lag," writes one equally-astonished player on the game's subreddit.

"Outside of having to spawn camp some wolves at the start, this has been the best wow launch I've seen so far. I haven't really had to compete for mobs, or herbs or quest drops, and I only had a brief moment of lag," writes another.

On that point, I do feel like the phasing is maybe working a little too well. I had an eerie experience jogging around Stormwind (admittedly, this was at 3 am on a Wednesday. Anyone with a normal job was likely sanely and soundly asleep) and having the Alliance's capital city all to myself.

But it is early days, with Blizzard clearly having braced hard to deal with its server capacity. And compared to the opposite of having to bare-knuckle wrestle people for quest tags—or group up and cooperate like some kind of loser, I guess—it's way more preferable. So kudos for Blizzard, managing a downright smooth MMO launch. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got some kobolds to rob of their candles.

#3711. Where Does Each 'Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' Couple Stand Before Season 6?

Several Secret Lives of Mormon Wives couples have been going through some changes off camera — but where does each couple stand before season 6?

When the show premiered on Hulu in 2024, viewers were introduced to Jen Affleck and husband Zac Affleck, Demi Engemann and husband Bret Engemann, Whitney Leavitt and husband Conner Leavitt, Mikayla Matthews and husband Jace Terry, Mayci Neeley and husband Jacob Neeley, Jessi Draper and husband Jordan Ngatikaura, Taylor Frankie Paul and then-partner Dakota Mortensen and Layla Taylor. (Miranda McWhorter later joined the show in season 2 after her split from Chase McWhorter.)

Demi and Whitney have since exited the show with their respective partners. The other couples have faced their fair share of ups and downs on screen — especially during season 5. The condensed season was released months after production was paused in May 2026 amid Taylor and Dakota’s domestic dispute.

Cameras picked back up again three months later to check in with everyone before they started filming season 6. Keep scrolling to see where the other couples stand at the end of season 5:

Throughout the seasons, Taylor and Dakota were together off-and-on while coparenting their son, Ever. Season 5 documented the aftermath of Taylor leading The Bachelorette season 22, during which she got engaged to Doug Mason. In March, news broke that Mormon Wives halted production after Taylor and Dakota were involved in a domestic violence dispute while filming.

They are currently not dating amid their legal back and forth.

While viewers know that Jessi and Jordan are no longer together, season 5 showed the couple still trying to make things work weeks before their divorce filing. Those closest to Jessi, however, made it clear they didn’t see her staying with Jordan for long.

Jessi is now dating Vanderpump Villa’s Marciano Brunette, who made a brief cameo in the fifth season of Mormon Wives.

Whitney and Conner made minimal appearances in season 5. Their family of five appeared to be thriving after relocating to New York City for Whitney’s Broadway run.

The first season of Mormon Wives highlighted the challenges in Jen and Zac’s marriage, which eventually led to an offscreen separation. They got back together before welcoming daughter Penelope in July 2025.

Season 5 showed Jen and Zac at odds over her career choices, such as investing in music equipment and considering a photo shoot for Sports Illustrated. Jen admitted she was once again questioning her future with Zac, which came months before she announced her pregnancy with baby No. 4.

In November 2026, TMZ reported that Jen had filed for divorce from Zac after seven years of marriage. Us reached out to reps for the pair for comment.

After welcoming their fourth baby, Mikayla and Jace decided to separate during season 4 of the hit Hulu series. Season 5 picked up with them back together after an offscreen reconciliation.

The duo have been married since 2018 and are parents of three. Jacob expressed interest in expanding their family again, but Mayci wasn’t as onboard with the idea despite her sister McCall DaPron — who is starring on the upcoming Mormon Wives OC spinoff — encouraging her to have more kids soon.

Layla’s relationship with Mason was brought up in season 5 when her friends questioned how much money she was spending on him — only for it not to be reciprocated. Layla mentioned it to Mason, and they broke up days later.

The reality star has since found love with Kelsie Chessner after coming out as bisexual.

It could be argued that the breakout star of You Can See Everything is Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans. He plays a big part in the documentary, which is the surprise hit of the 2026 movie schedule. The A24 release, co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, has a lot of WTF moments, and quite a few come from Evans. One of those moments comes when he admits that he’s been posting on X as Holmes from her account.

This week, Evans took to his own X account to do an AMA (Ask Me Anything), and one of the most-asked questions was about all the sniffling Evans was doing in the second half of the movie. He poked holes in one theory that fans brought up and insisted that he has been dealing with allergies since the movie Texas, where Holmes is serving her sentence in a Federal prison for her fraud convictions.

Evans answered a lot of questions over a couple of hours, and one question that came up multiple times in the AMA asked why he was sniffing so often. X user asked, and Evans responded that it was kids and allergies:

Solo parenting 2 toddlers, you are sick approx 75% of days. Allergies in Austin, TX are no joke. I take Claritin daily. Much less sniffling.

This was followed by another user asking if it was cocaine, and Evans was clear that it wasn’t, answering the user with “Never been a fan.” At another point, someone else asked the same question, and he had a similar response (along with a William Huang joke):

1) I love William Huang 2) I moved to Texas. The cedar here is no joke.

Evans also got into other things about You Can See Everything, including admitting that he does not regret making the movie, though he never answered a question as to why he and Holmes chose Fielder to direct the project. That’s a question even Fielder himself hasn’t been able to answer.

Evans also explained why, as he reveals in the movie, he has power of attorney over Holmes’ affairs. He was clear that it had nothing to do with posting from her X account (which he also insists Holmes is completely fine with), but rather to handle things on the outside while Holmes is serving her time. That is one of the things that actually makes sense to me.

It’s an interesting AMA, and I’d love to see Evans do it again. I’d really like to know more about what he thinks about the documentary, and if there is anything that was left out that frustrates him. He admits that a lot of footage was left on the cutting room floor, of course. In the meantime, I’ll continue tracking anything and everything about You Can See Everything, including all the reactions, its Oscar chances, and everything else.

#3708. Jen Affleck Files for Divorce From Zac While Pregnant With Baby No. 4

Jen Affleck has reportedly filed for divorce from her husband, Zac Affleck, just days before The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County premieres.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Jen, 27, reportedly filed a Tuesday, November 3, petition for divorce in Utah, where the pair wed. The Hulu reality star also submitted a proposed parenting plan, though the details of the filing are private.

The court records do not reveal the reason behind the breakup or Jen’s requested custody arrangements.

Us has reached out to reps for Jen and Zac, 30, for comment.

The couple — who announced in June that they are expecting baby No. 4 — met on the Mormon dating app Mutual in 2018 before getting engaged. They ultimately got married in 2019.

Jen and Zac’s love story was first put on display for the world to see when The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives premiered in September 2024. Since then, Hulu cameras have documented the pair struggling to keep their marriage strong and healthy.

Starting November 12, viewers will get another front-row seat into the state of their relationship when Jen appears on the spinoff show, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.

“We were so vulnerable, and we shared everything about our religion and our life and our marriage,” Zac said on a May 2025 episode of “The Viall Files” podcast. “I honestly think we went a little bit naive into the show — just not really knowing what to expect or what reality TV even is.”

Jen, however, always viewed reality TV as a way to confront life’s problems and make a change for the better.

“Sometimes you just feel called to something and you can’t explain why,” she detailed. “It’s not easy being vulnerable as a Mormon and showing what actually happens sometimes in Mormon relationships. I feel like we’re doing the hard thing but doing the right thing by exposing what actually happens.”

In a recent interview with People, Jen admitted that her marriage wasn’t as strong as she had hoped. At the same time, she remained hopeful that better days were ahead as she got used to life in Southern California.

“It’s been a lot the past couple of months, I’ll be honest,” Jen revealed to the publication in August. “But I do feel like I’m seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and just trying to count my blessings every single day.”

#3707. This New Garmin Feature Is Draining Battery Life, but There's a Quick Fix

Garmin users are taking to the company's support forums with a common grievance: The newly introduced "OK Garmin" hands-free voice feature appears to be eating through battery life. The feature arrived through Garmin’s September software updates, bringing hands-free voice activation to the Fenix 8, Forerunner 570 and 970, Venu 4, and several other models. Here's how to make sure Garmin's new updates aren't slashing your watch's battery life.

Last month's updates for select watches also brought all-day fall detection, a set of new Quick Workouts and Garmin Run Coach plans, as well as that "OK Garmin" hands-free voice command feature. It's exactly what it sounds like: Instead of pressing a button, users can simply say “OK Garmin” to activate voice commands. However, it looks like "OK Garmin" in particular is what causes some watch's projected runtimes to drastically drop, allegedly by roughly 35% to 50% in some cases.

Garmin does acknowledge that enabling these settings shortens battery life, though it doesn't say by how much. The tradeoff makes sense, since the watch has to listen constantly for its wake phrase. Even so, giving up several days of runtime is a steep price for a feature that many people may seldom use. Luckily, the fix is simple: Turning off "OK Garmin" should restore your battery life estimates right away.

If your watch has been draining faster since the update, go to Settings > System > Voice and disable "OK Garmin." If needed, you can also switch off the Phone Assistant wake word from the same area. The good news is that turning this feature off won't even take voice commands away—you can still trigger them manually using the watch's physical controls.

Keep in mind that these numbers are battery estimates rather than independently tested, real-world runtimes. Some of the battery complaints that surfaced after the update may also stem from unrelated issues. Still, trading away as much as half your battery life just to avoid pressing a button is a difficult bargain to defend.

#3706. Epic Games’ Tim Sweeney Insists AI Adoption ‘Unlikely To Be Reversed’ As Company Crams AI Into Unreal Engine 6

At Unreal Fest Tokyoâthe annual Epic Games event targeted at developers using the Unreal Engine technologyâthe company took to the stage to share updates about Unreal Engine 6, the somewhat controversial upgrade to its engine that puts a far greater emphasis on AI workflows. While developers have questioned Epic’s plans to remove the engine’s long-running workflows in place of AI assistants, the company doubled down on this, with CEO Tim Sweeney attending the event himself to defend the choice.

Detailing the differences between the current engine and the sixth version due for launch in 2027, Epic insisted on its plans to remove Blueprints from the engine. Blueprints are a workflow that many developers use to script how characters and events work within a game, and have existed in the engine for multiple decades. Epic promises âAI-assisted migrationâ as it moves away from this and other long-term systems.

Though Sweeney appeared on stage ostensibly to apologize for the decision, he insisted it’s a good thing. âWhile it will be painful at first, subsequent productivity will greatly improve,â the CEO told developers, based on a report of the event from Famitsu. Indeed, according to Sweeney, the use of AI in the engine could improve productivity up to four times that of development done without AI workflows.

âI believe weâre entering a very interesting era,â Sweeney said in comments made prior to his keynote speech, as reported by Denfaminico Gamer. âMajor shifts are already taking place, especially in game development, and the state of the game economy is also shifting at a fast pace. The driving force to this is the acceleration of almost everything caused by AI tools. A significant gap in competitive ability will grow between those that adopt AI tools and those that donât, and the adoption rate of tools is rising in places like China and South Korea. This trend is unlikely to be reversed.” He continued,

Considering this, we intend to maximize the acceleration of workflows using AI in Unreal Engine and use it to help make games even greater. The very nature of competitiveness in the gaming industry is set to undergo a fundamental shift, and I believe it is crucial that a wider variety of innovations emerge from and develop within Japan.

Recent years have seen more Japanese developers move away from internal engines to using Unreal, including Square Enix and Atlus. At the same time, some developers are cautious about the move, and differing opinions on the use of AI tools is a debate unlikely to subside any time soon. Epic Games is clearly set on AI being the future.

#3705. This Is the Robot Vacuum I Use Every Day, and It's 50% Off Right Now

I live in a 1,600-square-foot home, and vacuuming and mopping it by hand takes a considerable chunk of time. Passing that labor off to a robot vacuum was a great decision. I decided to go with the Roborock Qrevo CurvX since it seemed like a great fit for my circumstances. If you also have a dog, a mix of different floor types, and a gym with a workout mat, this robot vacuum might work for you, too. Amazon currently has it for $749.99 (originally $1,499.99), a 50% discount, and the lowest price it has ever been, according to price-tracking tools.

One of the main things I was looking for in a robot vacuum was suction power. The Qrevo CurvX has 22,000 Pa, which is stronger than most options at its price and is powerful enough to pick up anything that needs vacuuming in my house. I like that it has a self-lifting chassis so it can climb over my workout mat, rugs, obstacles like cables, or anything else that might be in the way, so I don't have to babysit it while it's doing its job. I also like the extendable mop pads and side brushes that allow it to reach corners and crevices it might not be slim enough to fit into. (Speaking of which, it's only 3.14 inches tall, so it can fit under most couches and beds without issue.)

My experience with the Roborock app has been great. It's easy to use and gives me enough control to clean my house how I want without a hassle. "No Go Zones" are easy to set up, as is the schedule. The main issue I've had is the size of the internal dust bin: It's small, so it needs to be cleaned after basically every scheduled use (though that shouldn't be as bad if you don't have a pet that sheds a lot).

Take it from me: If you're looking for a reliable hybrid robot vacuum that can clean multiple types of floors, mop, and comes with a great app, the Qrevo CurvX makes a compelling case at the current $750 discount.

#3704. Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' Jen and Zac Affleck's Relationship Timeline

Viewers have a lot of opinions about Jen Affleck and Zac Affleck‘s marriage after watching their relationship play out on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.

The couple started dating in 2018 and got married one year later. After expanding their family twice, Jen and Zac joined the cast of Hulu’s reality series The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, which followed a group of Mormon mom influencers in Utah. Season 1 showed Jen and Zac nearly calling it quits before admitting they were still a work in progress.

“Ever since we finished filming, we’ve been doing nonstop therapy and it’s been great,” Jen exclusively told Us Weekly in September 2024 after the series premiered. “So if anything, [watching the show] is just going to be exposure therapy at this point. We’ve healed and now we’re ready to talk about it once it comes out.”

Jen also denied that her husband had anything to do with her leaving MomTok, saying, “It had a lot to do with just me and just figuring out everything. There are so many factors — not just our relationship — like religion, friendships and my children.”

She continued: “In order to make the right decision for me and my family, I really had to take a step back and ask myself, ‘How am I going to move forward and what’s best for us?’ You’ll just have to wait for season 2 to see what happens.”

That same month, Jen praised Zac for how he supported her — emotionally and monetarily — since they started dating.

“Zac bought me my first laptop when he had $10 in his bank account. When I shared my dream of running a marathon, he trained alongside me and ran it with me. I told him I wanted to start my videography business, so he saved up money and bought me my first camera. When we were expecting our first baby, I wanted a place to call home, so he worked hard, saved up, and bought us our first house,” she wrote via Instagram at the time. “He gave me both stability and freedom, which allowed me to post videos online and launch my career on social media. This, in turn allowed me to support him and our family while he’s been in school.”

Jen noted she “couldn’t have” found success on her own without Zac by her side.

“Is Zac perfect? No. Does he have flaws that we’ve needed to address? Yes. But I can confidently say he’s always supported and believed in me more than anyone else,” she continued. “We’re still young, we have two precious babies, and we still have struggles like so many marriages. But do we love each other? Yes. Are we willing to put in the work to be better? Yes. Have there been moments when we wanted to walk away? Of course. But there’s so much more to our marriage and what we offer to each other than people realize.”

After Hulu renewed The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives for season 2, viewers questioned the status of Jen and Zac’s marriage. The pair took a step back from sharing highlights from their relationship once they made the move from Utah to New York so Zac could attend medical school.

Keep scrolling to relive Jen and Zac’s relationship before — and after — The Secret Wives of Mormon Wives:

Jen and Zac started dating in 2018 after meeting on Mormon dating app Mutual. After one year of dating, Zac proposed at Top of the Rock in New York City.

The duo tied the knot in 2019 at a local The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints temple.

“I knew Zac was the one when I realized I couldn’t imagine life without him & his amazing qualities,” Jen wrote via Instagram ahead of their wedding ceremony. “I’m grateful to have someone who loves me unconditionally, puts me first, & makes me want to be a better fiancé, friend, daughter and person. Can’t forget he makes me the happiest girl alive.”

Zac and Jen welcomed their first child, daughter Nora, in November 2021. The reality star reflected on the milestone moment three years later, writing via Instagram, “Nora brings so much joy and light into our lives, and I feel incredibly blessed to be her mom 🥺 There are countless things that I adore about her — she’s spunky, kind, and full of life. … To us, she truly is everything.”

“Three years ago today I made the best decision of my life. That was to marry my best friend. It was a day we’ll always remember,” Jen gushed on social media. “To be surrounded by everyone we love, promising each other the world, we were so excited to start this new adventure. I wish I could relive every second of this day. It truly was a DREAM.”

Jen and Zac’s son, Lucas, was born in July 2023.

“We were so young when we first became parents, with lots to learn, but Zac has always been there every step of the way,” Jen wrote via Instagram in honor of Father’s Day in 2024. “He’s never wavered in giving Nora and Luca everything they need.”

Zac and Jennifer weathered some public storms when season 1 of The Secret Wives of Mormon Wives premiered on Hulu. Initially, Jen was presented as a more conservative Mormon, but it wasn’t until the end of the season that her costars — and viewers — got a glimpse at her marital issues when Zac told her she had “no values or morals” for enjoying a girls’ night out in Las Vegas.

Jen’s costar Demi Engemann claimed she saw text messages in which Zac threatened to end their marriage, said he didn’t love her anymore and made his wife come to his hotel room in the middle of the night to work out their problems. Demi also accused Zac of having a gambling problem, which is forbidden by the Mormon church.

“I think that there was a lot of things that Jen was doing at the time — and I think she would admit this — that were kind of driven by Zac’s insecurities,” Demi told Us at the time “I really do feel like she has found her voice. She’s now, like, ‘Hey, we are individuals as well as a couple. I have every right to do what feels right for me too within certain boundaries and respect for the relationship.’ But I think she has found her voice and I’m excited to see how that dynamic shifts.”

Costar Jessi Ngatikaura, meanwhile, questioned “the influence” Zac had on Jennifer.

“He’s the man of the house and has a lot of opinions on things,” Jessi noted to Us. “So I don’t think Jen would ever make that decision [to leave] on her own because she loves the friend group and she loves being around us. I would say that he definitely has a lot of influence on her decisions.”

The pair didn’t just make headlines because of their rocky marriage. After Zac claimed on screen that he was actor Ben Affleck‘s second cousin, fans and costars alike questioned the validity of that connection.

“I don’t think Jen would lie about that. I really don’t, but maybe [Zac] could. I mean, we’ve seen a little bit of how he can be,” Jessi said on Scheana Shay’s “Scheananigans” podcast. “But also maybe Ben Affleck’s team’s like, ‘We want nothing to do with you guys.’ So let’s dig and, like, plant this story because Zac is looking a little bad.”

Jessi noted that Jen and Zac “made the last name such a thing.” Reports later surfaced that Jen and Zac are not related to Ben, which they have not addressed. Jen previously told Us that she never crossed paths with Ben.

“We’ve never met him,” she said in September 2024. “Zac’s dad has, a long time ago. Hopefully we meet him sometime soon because we are family.”

Despite social media backlash about her marriage, Jen stood by Zac.

“I definitely think it was the best thing to happen to our relationship. While watching the show, a lot of people are going to think that maybe this would break our relationship apart. But if anything, it did the opposite,” Jen explained to Us when asked how the show impacted her marriage. “Being on camera and having those moments happen made us take a step back and actually look at a relationship and make us just see what we have to change.”

Jen took to Instagram to share a message reflecting on the highlights from her relationship with Zac.

“We were just kids when we got married. Young, naive, and inexperienced, we truly had no idea what we were getting ourselves into. Coming from completely different backgrounds, families, and upbringings, it didn’t seem to make sense. We were polar opposites,” she captioned the post. “How could we make this work? How could we see the same picture?”

Jen admitted that the twosome aren’t always on the same page, adding, “We didn’t always see eye to eye, and a lot of times, we still don’t. But that’s what marriage is, we keep trying. I truly believe there were lessons we both needed to teach each other.”

Jen sparked split speculation when she shared multiple TikTok videos that clearly showed her missing a ring on her left hand. Jen didn’t address the rumors but Zac was still featured in posts across her various social media platforms.

Hulu renewed The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives for a second season one month after the show premiered. Jen and Zac moved from Utah to New York once filming started, which left their status with the show unclear.

“Choosing to step away from social media has been one of the best things I’ve done for my mental health,” Jen wrote via Instagram Story. “I can’t lie — these months have been some of the toughest I’ve faced, but they’ve also helped me gain clarity about myself, my relationships and the mother and friend I aspire to be.”

Zac, meanwhile, kept his Instagram account private while his bio read, “Official Fan Page of Jen, Nora and Luca @jenniferlaffleck.”

Jen announced she is pregnant and expecting her third baby with Zac later this year.

“I’ve always dreamed of a big family, and seeing that dream come true is both exciting and fulfilling,” Jen shared with People. “It can be daunting to think about raising three babies while pursuing my career, but I want to show women and mothers that they can achieve anything they set their minds to, no matter how unrealistic it may seem.”

During an episode of “The Viall Files,” Jen and Zac first broke down what led them to reality TV — and revealed how the experience almost ruined their relationship.

“We were so vulnerable and we shared everything about our religion and our life and our marriage,” Zac said. “I honestly think we went a little bit naive into the show — just not really knowing what to expect or what reality TV even is.”

Jen, meanwhile, expressed hope that her involvement in the show would start a conversation. “Sometimes you just feel called to something and you can’t explain why,” she detailed. “It’s not easy being vulnerable as a Mormon and showing what actually happens sometimes in Mormon relationships. I feel like we’re doing the hard thing but doing the right thing by exposing what actually happens.”

She continued: “Hopefully people within the Mormon culture can look at our relationship and reflect on theirs and say like, ‘Hey, I think we kind of struggle with that too. Or maybe my husband has fed into the patriarchy and isn’t treating me right.’ I want to be an example of that. People aren’t going to like that, unfortunately.”

Elsewhere in the episode, Zac explained why he was surprised by Jen’s second pregnancy. “We had one and then a second baby back to back. Jen — like, six months after she gave birth — she got pregnant again with her second baby,” he said before claiming, “I got tricked into it. She took out her IUD without telling me.”

Zac called that period of time “stressful” and noted it was before they got into therapy. Jen, meanwhile, found the revelation about her second pregnancy more funny, adding, “Whoopsies, I forgot to tell you [I took my IUD out].”

“This year has tested us in ways I never imagined, yet somehow we found a way to come out stronger than before,” Jen wrote for her and Zac’s anniversary.

The couple welcomed their third baby, daughter Penelope, days later. “She is perfect,” Jen wrote via Instagram on Wednesday, July 2. “Going unmedicated was truly the most painful but empowering experience of my life. I could not have done it without Zac and my supportive doula! I’m so grateful and so happy that Penny is earth side now.”

Jen announced via Instagram that she and Zac are expecting their fourth baby.

“Chapter Four. 🤍,” she wrote alongside a photo of herself cradling her baby bump.

Five months after Jen announced her pregnancy with baby No. 4, TMZ reported that she filed for divorce from Zac. Us reached out to reps for the pair for comment.

#3702. The Garmin Cirqa Finally Got a Much-Needed Feature

This week Garmin's screenless Cirqa smart band received a firmware update that fixes one of its most obvious gaps: the lack of alerts from your phone. With Version 4.20, you can now set up your smart band to buzz your wrist for texts, calls, and other smart notifications from your phone. The addition is listed on Garmin's forums as "Support vibration for smart notifications/incoming calls." Reaction has been upbeat, too—users on the Garmin subreddit have been glad to see the feature arrive.

Amusingly, Garmin's own FAQ still states that the Cirqa does not vibrate for text messages, phone calls, or other smartphone notifications. Clearly that page is now out of date, so Garmin will want to correct it. Since Garmin doesn't yet have step-by-step instructions, I tested the text-message vibrations myself. Here's how you can set up your Cirqa smart band to vibrate for calls and texts, in addition to a number of other promising updates to check out.

To receive these alerts, your band must be running firmware 4.20 or later. Here is how to get everything configured.

Update the firmware. Open your Garmin Connect app and sync your Cirqa, so the app can check for and install version 4.20 or newer.

Grant the necessary phone permissions. In your phone's settings, make sure Garmin Connect has permission to access SMS, Contacts, and Phone.

Configure notifications in Garmin Connect. Back in Garmin Connect, tap the Menu (or More) tab. Select Garmin Devices, then choose your Cirqa Smart Band. Go to Notifications & Alerts (or Smart Notifications) and turn on text and call alerts.

Troubleshooting tip: If alerts aren't coming through, check that Do Not Disturb, Sleep Mode, and any aggressive Battery Saver settings are turned off on both your phone and the band.

For most a lot of Cirqa fans, the phone alerts are the headline, but the 4.20 update carries a solid list of other improvements and bug fixes:

Trail Run: Run/Walk detection is now available for Trail Run activities.

Timestamp fix: Resolved a problem where an activity's recorded time didn't match the time on your phone.

Distance calibration: You can now calibrate distance for Treadmill Run, Indoor Rowing, and Indoor Cycling before saving the activity on the device.

Duration alerts: Duration time alerts for speaking out now accumulate.

Stress alerts: Stress alerts are now blocked while Auto Activity Detection is recording.

Bedtime reminders: Fixed an issue where the bedtime approaching notification sometimes failed to trigger.

Live Activity: Heart rate now appears on the Live Activity screen before recording begins.

Pinned activity bug: Fixed an issue where the pinned activity reverted to Timed Activity after changing the phone's language.

Workout editing: Fixed a problem that prevented editing reps during a workout.

Stability: General system stability improvements.

From finalized divorces to ongoing separations, scroll below to see which Mormon Wives couples have called it quits since the series’ premiere:

Jordan Ngatikaura filed for divorce from Jessi Draper in March 2026, months after her emotional cheating scandal with fellow Hulu star Marciano Brunette while filming Vanderpump Villa.

Jessi and Jordan, who share son Jagger and daughter Jovi, signed off on their divorce paperwork in September 2026, closing the book on five years of marriage.

Taylor Frankie Paul and Dakota Mortensen’s on-again, off-again relationship exploded into a custody war in 2026. The exes, who welcomed son Ever in March 2024, split for good in fall 2025 before Taylor filmed The Bachelorette season 22. (Taylor’s season was scrapped by ABC over resurfaced footage from her 2023 arrest.)

Halloween is finally here, and plenty of people like to watch some spooky content as a result. In addition to the best horror movies, there are also seasonal favorites like Practical Magic (with the original streaming with an HBO Max subscription). I took the time to finally watch its sequel, and now I'm mad about its poor reviews.

Practical Magic 2's reviews were pretty poor, despite how long fans waited for the book-to-screen adaptation to return to the big screen. At first, I thought it was possible that the sequel didn't deliver the same charm as its predecessor, but after watching it for myself, I think that critics were way too hard on Susanne Bier's movie.

The first Practical Magic suffered from poor reviews, and history unfortunately repeated itself with the second film. In fact, Practical Magic 2's Rotten Tomatoes score is sitting at a dismal 36%. I originally gave reviewers the benefit of the doubt, but after seeing the movie myself I think folks were way too hard on it.

Obviously there were high expectations for Practical Magic 2, and it's impossible to match the same charm as the original cult classic. Still, I thought the long-awaited sequel was still a super enjoyable ride. Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman's chemistry is electric, as is the bond between Joey King and Maisie Williams as Sally's daughters.

For what it's worth, I'm not alone here. The Rotten Tomatoes audience score is a glowing 90%. This isn't the first time fans and critics disagreed, but that's quite the discrepancy. Now I'm feeling way less crazy about how much I enjoyed Practical Magic 2.

From the minute I heard the franchise's theme song and saw the Owens house in the sequel, I was hit with nostalgic feels. It felt great seeing Kidman and Bullock together on the big screen, especially since they also reunited with the great Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest. Unfortunately, the latter's character, Jet, died fairly early into its runtime

On top of the charming fun of the movie, I was moved by its story about grief and loneliness. The stakes of the movie felt higher than its predecessor, but Practical Magic 2 still brought everything that fans of the original were hoping for. That includes midnight margaritas, plenty of spells, and the Owens women jumping off of the roof with their umbrellas.

Having seen a bunch of long-awaited sequels that were actually awful (I'm looking at you, Independence Day: Resurgence), I'm a little tiffed that this one got such a bad rap. Luckily, audiences agree with me, and I have to assume plenty of fans will be watching it to celebrate the end of spooky season.

Practical Magic 2 is available to rent and purchase now digitally as part of the 2026 movie release list. If you were curious about the movie, don't let the poor reviews discourage you!

#3698. You Can Get This 65-Inch Toshiba Mini-LED TV for $550 Right Now

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Amazon has dropped the price of the 65-inch Toshiba Z670R to $549.97 from $748.99, taking nearly $200 off and bringing it to its lowest price ever, according to price trackers. The deal also includes free delivery to a room of your choice, which normally costs $19.99, though it does not cover unpacking, setup, packaging removal, or haul-away services. You also get a 90-day free trial of Amazon Music with your purchase.

Beyond the discounts, the Z670R has quite a bit going for it, starting with a 4K Mini-LED panel that combines QLED color with local dimming to help bright highlights stand out without washing out darker scenes. It also supports Dolby Vision IQ and HDR10+, so you can enjoy compatible HDR content across a wide range of movies, shows, and streaming services.

Gaming is another area where this TV makes a strong case for itself—its panel can run at up to 144Hz, while Variable Refresh Rate, Auto Low Latency Mode, and AMD FreeSync Premium are there to keep fast movement looking smoother and cut down on screen tearing with a compatible console or gaming PC, making it well-suited for racing games, shooters, and sports titles. You also get four HDMI inputs, with support for 4K at 144Hz, so there is room for a console, PC, soundbar, and another device without constantly swapping cables.

Fire TV is built in as well, which means Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, and other major streaming apps are available without adding a separate streaming stick, while Alexa handles voice searches and basic controls. The built-in audio is also more substantial than what you get from many slim TVs, with a dedicated bass woofer and Dolby Atmos support, so you may be able to live without a soundbar at first if you are setting up a bedroom or smaller living room. One potential downside is that Mini-LED does not give you the perfect blacks of OLED, so movie fans who watch mostly in a dark room may still prefer to pay more for one. For someone who splits time between movies, sports, and gaming, though, the Z670R gives you a lot of flexibility for about $550 without immediately requiring extra equipment.

There have been plenty of movies I’ve seen in recent memory that have catered or mostly catered to a female audience. I’m not just talking about movies like Barbie. It Ends with Us was like that. So was The Housemaid, though the latter did have some testosterone in the room. Doubtless The Devil Wears Prada would have been similar had I managed to catch it in theaters. The experience of seeing a movie in a roomful of women isn’t that weird these days, but I can 100% say seeing Wicker in a packed theater of women was a wild experience. I can't recommend it enough.

Listen, I’ve been in some invested audiences before. I bawled my eyes out in The Fault in our Stars. I was in a giant theater opening night and the whole crowd burst into applause several times when Godzilla opened in 2014. I saw Twilight: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 in an early screening before the fanbase knew what was coming and people in the theater were freaking out. Some fans literally stood up several times in my Avengers: Endgame showing. None of this prepared me for the crowd I’d sit with during my viewing of Wicker this weekend.

I can’t remember the last time I sat with such a rowdy crowd. Actually, that’s not true. I can. It was Magic Mike.

Let me set the stage really quickly. Wicker is in wide release right now, but with You Can See Everything, Clayface and more in theaters, it’s not exactly occupying prime real estate. At my local theater, we were in the last theater in a row of theaters, and there were maybe 40 seats in total. (I just checked; it’s 44.) Despite these uphill battles, outside of a few first row strays, my entire theater was full, and entirely full of women. It was the perfect crowd.

If you’ve seen Wicker, it manages an oddball tone that’s both sincere and extremely funny, and on top of this just the general idea of Alexander Skarsgard being recreated in wicker lends even more absurdity to any viewing of the movie. Critics have loved Wicker, but also It’s no wonder the sex scenes were so difficult to pull off.

The audience was primed for this. As characters died and Wicker babies were born (created?), everyone in the room was vocal. The laughter was palpable. Many times people hooted and hollered at the screen. Everyone was very invested in Mr. Wicker, the undeniably awesome character played by Alexander Skarsgard, a creature who upended the village just by figuring out how how to communicate with the woman he loved.

It's subversive, sex positive, and hilarious, and I feel completely justified in saying I think it has to be better in exactly the context I watched it in: A packed theater chock full of women.

I haven’t seen Wicker from the comfort of my own couch yet, for obvious reasons. Doubtless it will still have a wicked script and will still be received positively by audiences, but this is one rare indie movie that absolutely translates to the movie theater and deserves a solid box office run; I feel confident it will NOT be better from the comfort of your own home. I feel so grateful a bunch of ladies threw on their sweatshirts and brought in their theater blankets on a Sunday evening to experience Wicker with me.

I’m as enamored with you all as I was with Mr. Skarsgård and the sacrifices he made to turn his body into wood on the big screen.

#3696. Heidi Klum Shocks In Severed Hand Halloween Costume

Heidi Klum has done it again. The Project Runway host exceeded all our Halloween expectations by transforming herself into a giant, severed human hand nearly two meters tall for the latest edition of her annual party, held Saturday night in New York City. The costume, which required hours of work by her makeup and prop team, left no detail to chance: hyper-realistic veins modeled after her own anatomy, wrinkles, red-painted nails, and an exxagerated version of the rings she typically wears.

“Mike [Marino, from the special effects team ProRenFX] has all of these scans of my body, so he was able to use those to create an exact replica of my hand,” Klum explained to Vogue. “We wanted everything to be as realistic as possible—the anatomy, the veins, the muscles, all the little details that make a hand look like a real hand.”

The costume’s structure used the model's legs to form two of the fingers, while her right arm provided mobility for the thumb. Only her eyes and mouth were visible amid the bloody wounds on her palm, from which—to top off the gruesomeness of it all—Heidi Klum would occasionally spit out the fake blood that a team of assistants injected into her mouth. The most macabre part was at the wrist, where a horrific gash exposed a jumble of blood, bones, and torn flesh.

Heidi Klum (L) recieves an injection of fake blood to augment her 2026 Halloween costume.

Other guests at Klum's party included Kyle MacLachlan, who arrived dressed as his character from The Flintstones; Neil Patrick Harris and his husband David Burtka, dressed as the girls from The Shining; and Heidi Klum and Flavio Briatore's daughter, Leni Klum.

Before making her grand entrance, the host had built up anticipation on social media by posting clues about this year’s costume, such as a photo of her real hand that showed her wedding ring alongside the small tattoo of husband Tom Kaulitz's name. It, too, was part of her Halloween costume. “Nothing was overlooked! I love that Mike pays attention to things that most people might not even notice at first. The details make these costumes so special. It’s not just any giant hand: It’s my giant hand!” Klum said.

Heidi Klum 2026 Halloween costume, as seen from the back.

This is the 25th annual Halloween party thrown by the former Victoria’s Secret Angel: The event began in 2000, and has only continued to expand in scope. “ “Can you believe it? Twenty-five years of Halloween, costumes, incredible transformations, and so many amazing memories,” she said.

Last night’s “amputated hand” joins Klum's collection of Halloween costumes that ranges from last year’s mythological Medusa (with a petrified Kaulitz by her side) to E.T., to Shrek’s Fiona, to a disgusting giant worm inside which she feared she might suffocate. We're already looking forward to what she comes up with for next year.
